### Record: agents/frobenius/E3_explicit_walker_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit of the specified generic Walker counterexample

## Outcome

The proof of E.3r in research/agents/cycles/explicit_walker_counterexample.tex passes this independent proof and primary-source audit. It specifies the generic fourfold and the exact Legendre point of order two, and gives a mathematically exact selection rule for the auxiliary integral cycle. It does not give polynomial equations for that auxiliary cycle. The construction is a function-field example over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, subsequently embedded in the complex numbers.

The only suggested clarification concerns the quantifier over embeddings. If the statement intends one selected cycle gamma to work for every embedding K into C, the proof should explicitly add the intrinsic mod-two étale-cohomology argument below. This is a valid strengthening of the written proof, not an obstruction to its conclusion for a fixed embedding.

## 1. Geometry of the family and integral parity transfer

There are exactly 72 independent coefficients: two rows, three columns, two monomials in the first projective-line coordinates, and six quadratic monomials in the appropriate projective-plane coordinates. The first-row zero scheme has degree 12 because the degree of (h+2l)^3 on P1 times P2 is 12. On an open set where the threefold is smooth and this scheme is finite étale, its product with the second projective plane is an effective Cartier divisor. One may choose this open to contain an Ottem–Suzuki rational matrix having their parity obstruction.

The relative Hilbert argument preserves integral coefficients. A curve over the complex realization of the generic coefficient tuple gives a point of a finite-type relative Hilbert scheme whose image in the coefficient space, considered as a Qbar-scheme, is the generic point. An irreducible Hilbert component containing that point therefore dominates the coefficient open. Its proper image is closed, so it has a point over the chosen Ottem–Suzuki matrix. The special subscheme has a one-cycle with integral multiplicities; no irreducibility of that special subscheme is required. Degrees against the two specified line bundles are constant in the flat Hilbert family, by the constancy of Euler characteristics. Embedded and zero-dimensional components do not contribute to these degrees. Thus the parity congruence transfers with coefficient one. There is no finite-cover trace or extension-degree multiplier.

The current wording, “one-cycle with integral multiplicities,” correctly avoids confusing an integral-coefficient cycle with an irreducible curve.

## 2. The defect class, its minimal multiple, and descent

Parallel transport of the Ottem–Suzuki integral homology class along the connected smooth coefficient open preserves its two intersections, one and zero. Their torsion-freeness result applies to the integral cohomology. Their H2(O)=0 assertion, Hodge decomposition, and hard Lefschetz make every rational fourth-cohomology class algebraic and every integral fourth-cohomology class a Hodge class. Thus the algebraic subgroup B has finite index in the torsion-free lattice H4.

Let m be the least positive integer with m beta in B. The transferred parity condition forces m to be even. If m beta were in 2B, torsion-freeness of H4 would imply that (m/2) beta belongs to B, contrary to minimality. Therefore m beta tensor 1/2 is nonzero in B tensor Q/Z, while its image in H4 tensor Q/Z is zero. Any algebraic representative gamma consequently has gamma tensor 1/2 nonzero in CH2(W) tensor Q/Z.

The descent of gamma to the algebraically closed coefficient field k is valid. For each integral component in a complex representative, take a component of the Hilbert scheme of the fixed k-variety containing that geometric point and then a k-point on it. Over an algebraically closed field, the relevant reduced irreducible components are geometrically irreducible. Connecting points by curves in such a component gives algebraic equivalence of the corresponding integral cycles, hence preserves integral cohomology classes. No norm is needed and no integer is introduced.

For a single gamma to work under every embedding, use the following intrinsic formulation. Its nonzero class in CH2(W/k) tensor Q/Z has already been established over k. Its mod-two étale cycle class is zero over k, because smooth proper base change identifies that group with the mod-two comparison group under the embedding used to construct gamma. Hence its cycle class is even under every complex embedding. Schoen injectivity and the Deligne calculation then apply unchanged under each embedding. This supplies the optional uniform-embedding clarification.

## 3. Exact Schoen theorem and the selected point of order two

We directly opened the local primary PDF and viewed the theorem on printed p.177. Schoen's Theorem (0.2) assumes precisely: k and K algebraically closed, W smooth proper over k, E a genus-one curve over K with j-invariant transcendental over k. Its injectivity statement is for CH(W) tensor CH(E)tors as a whole. It does not remove the prime two and does not single out a special torsion direction.

For the specified Legendre equation, the discriminant is 16 t^2(1-t)^2 and its j-invariant is the nonconstant rational function 256(1-t+t^2)^3/[t^2(1-t)^2]. Transcendence of t over k gives the required transcendence of j. The difference (0,0)-infinity is a nonzero point of exact order two. Any such point is the image of 1/2 in a direct summand Q/Z of the elliptic torsion group (Q/Z)^2: extend that nonzero vector in the two-torsion subgroup to a basis of the divisible torsion group. Consequently gamma tensor tau is nonzero, and Schoen's theorem makes its exterior product nonzero of exact order two.

## 4. Deligne cohomology and Walker torsion injectivity

The Deligne sequence has divisible kernel J2(W). The tensor product of a divisible group with a torsion group is zero. Right exactness of tensoring therefore identifies the tensor product of H_D^4 with the elliptic torsion group with the corresponding tensor product of the integral Hodge lattice. Multiplicativity of the Deligne cycle class sends the exterior product through this latter tensor product. Its value is m beta tensor tau, which is zero because m is even. Thus the product is Abel–Jacobi trivial. This is exactly the mechanism in Suzuki's Proposition 3.1, author pp.5–6, now checked for the specified field and elliptic point.

Ottem–Suzuki Lemma 2.4 gives CH0(W_C)=Z. Moving each point of a fibre W times {e'} to the fixed point w0 shows that CH0(W times E) is supported on {w0} times E. Suzuki Theorem 1.1, author p.2, applies to a smooth projective variety whose CH0 is supported on a subvariety of dimension at most three and to codimension p in {3,dim(X)-1}. Both conditions hold for this fourfold in codimension three. Its Walker map is injective on algebraically trivial torsion. The nonzero two-torsion exterior product therefore has nonzero Walker image and is not in the zero-cycle-generated relation N.

The already audited family-converse theorem E.3j applies to this same fourfold, so the indicated example does refute the literal integral biconditional. It does not close or alter the separate general Walker-generation equality.

## Primary-source opening ledger

1. Ottem, J. C., and Suzuki, F. (2020). A pencil of Enriques surfaces with non-algebraic integral Hodge classes. Primary author PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.08994 . Opened in full through the web tool and read locally at research/agents/cycles/sources/OttemSuzuki2020.pdf. Checked Lemmas 2.3–2.7, author pp.4–6; Theorem 3.1, pp.6–8; parity equation (1), p.7; and the integral homology class, p.8. Retrieval refs: turn125996541view0 and turn663610137view0.

Retrieval refs: turn125996541view1 and turn663610137view1.

3. Schoen, C. (2000). On certain exterior product maps of Chow groups. Mathematical Research Letters, 7, 177–194. Primary publisher URL: https://intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/mrl/2000/0007/0002/MRL-2000-0007-0002-a004.pdf . The web-tool request returned HTTP 403 and is not counted as a successful web opening. The independently acquired local primary PDF research/agents/cycles/sources/Schoen2000Exterior.pdf was read and its printed p.177 was rendered and visually checked. ### Record: agents/frobenius/E3_family_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit of E.3m–n

**Auditor:** GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), agent /root/frobenius.  
**Date:** 19 November 2026.  
**Files checked:** agents/cycles/family_converse_reduction.tex and agents/cycles/family_countability.tex.  
**Outcome:** E.3m passes. E.3n passes after the moving-lemma notation was corrected; we also read the replacement Hilbert-scheme paragraph.

## E.3m: the exact Walker quotient

We checked the proof without assuming that its abstract quotient \(E\) carries a universal integral family. The original family on \(B\), its quotient by the connected kernel of the Walker map, and then its quotient by a finite subgroup are algebraic maps. Only the resulting injection \(E(\mathbb C)\to P\) initially remains an abstract homomorphism.

On enlarging the family from \(B\) to \(B\times A\), the map \(B\to E'\) remains algebraic. Its kernel contains the kernel of \(B\to E\) because both maps into \(P\) agree and \(E'(\mathbb C)\to P\) is injective. In characteristic zero these are reduced subgroup schemes, so the equality on complex points supplies the scheme-theoretic kernel containment needed for quotient descent. Hence \(E\to E'\) is algebraic. Its pointwise injectivity and equal dimensions make it an isomorphism. The enlargement argument therefore shows that a single image contains every abelian-family image.

The finite-family covering of the Walker Jacobian is also valid: each family has an abelian-subvariety image, finite sums remain abelian subvarieties, and strict enlargements increase dimension. Surjectivity of the Walker map together with the integral abelian parameterization of E.3g forces the terminal sum to be the whole Jacobian.

It follows that \(\ker(P\to J_W)\) is finite. It is a quotient of the divisible group \(\ker\psi_W\), so it is divisible and hence zero. We reopened Achter, Casalaina-Martin, and Vial (2022), Theorem 2.3, author manuscript p. 12, which is exactly the divisibility assertion required. No universality statement for arbitrary regular homomorphisms is substituted for this assertion.

The optional direct regularity argument also passes. If the integral map \(v:\operatorname{Alb}(T)(\mathbb C)\to E(\mathbb C)\) satisfies \(mv=f\) with \(f\) algebraic, then \(f\) kills the finite group scheme \(\operatorname{Alb}(T)[m]\). Thus \(f=g\circ[m]\) algebraically. The difference \(v-g\) has finite image and divisible source, so vanishes. Smooth projective compactification and closure of the cycle then handle quasi-projective parameter varieties; local constructions agree as morphisms because the target is separated.

## E.3n: countability with integral Albanese relations

### Correction identified and implemented

The original text asserted a map
\[
\mathrm{CH}_0(T^\circ)\longrightarrow\mathrm{CH}_0(T)
\]
for an open immersion. Such a pushforward is not defined in general. For example \(\mathrm{CH}_0(\mathbb A^1)=0\) while \(\mathrm{CH}_0(\mathbb P^1)=\mathbb Z\).

The needed statement is instead that every class in \(\mathrm{CH}_0(T)\) has a representative supported in \(T^\circ\), equivalently that \(Z_0(T^\circ)\to\mathrm{CH}_0(T)\) is surjective. The given curve-and-Riemann–Roch proof proves this integral representative statement. The cycles agent corrected the notation before this audit was closed.

### Parameter spaces

We checked that each operation uses finite discrete choices, indexed by countably many integers or Hilbert polynomials. Parameter varieties \(T\) can be embedded in projective spaces of varying dimensions; their smooth geometrically connected loci are obtained on finite-type strata. A marked point supplies a section.

The relative Albanese input was reopened in Javanpeykar and Mathur (2022), Theorem 2.2 and its following paragraph. It gives arbitrary-base-change compatibility for smooth proper characteristic-zero families, with the marked section turning the torsor into the pointed group scheme. Consequently the weighted Albanese-zero condition is an actual closed condition.

For correspondence cycles, the restriction to points of a common fibre-flat open is legitimate after the moving step. Vertical components act trivially because the zero-cycle can be represented away from their images. Relative Hilbert schemes parameterize the remaining flat families; fibre-flat loci are constructible, and finite stratification supplies cycle maps into fixed Chow schemes. These conditions retain integer multiplicities and do not replace the Albanese kernel by its saturation.

### Rational-equivalence witnesses

We read the revised argument using integral subschemes of \(\mathbb P^1\times X\), rather than a universal cycle over a Chow scheme. An integral subscheme dominating \(\mathbb P^1\) is flat over that regular curve. Its two fibre cycles differ by a rational equivalence. Conversely, closing the graph of a rational function produces precisely such a witness, with integral multiplicities. The Stacks Project, Lemma 43.9.1, Tag 0AZI, was opened and gives this exact equivalence, including the norm for generically finite projection to the cycle's support.

All finite signed sums of witnesses are parameterized by products of Hilbert schemes; endpoint equality is imposed in a fixed Chow scheme. Chevalley's theorem then gives countably many constructible image sets. We also reopened Schoen (1993), Lemma 4.4 and its proof, pp. 311–313, and checked its Hilbert–Chow witness construction. The additional relative Albanese-zero condition is supplied by this new proof, not attributed to Schoen.

### Uniform exponent and conclusion

The countably constructible sets for all positive exponents cover a nonempty open of the abelian variety if every family value is torsion. Baire gives a dense constructible member and thus a nonempty Zariski open \(V\) on which one fixed exponent kills the map. The kernel is a subgroup and \(V-V=A(\mathbb C)\), since any two translates of a nonempty open meet in an irreducible variety. Hence the same exponent kills the whole homomorphism. Divisibility of \(A(\mathbb C)\) then makes that homomorphism zero.

No uniform exponent is assumed in advance. The proof is integral and specific to the stated complex setting. Its final combination with E.3c and E.3m is an equivalence of remaining gates, not a proof that those gates always hold.

## Opened primary sources

- Achter, J. D., Casalaina-Martin, S., & Vial, C. (2022). *The Walker Abel–Jacobi map descends*. Theorem 2.3, author p. 12. https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~vial/WalkerAJmap.pdf
- Javanpeykar, A., & Mathur, S. (2022). *Smooth hypersurfaces in abelian varieties over arithmetic rings*. Theorem 2.2 and following paragraph. https://doi.org/10.1017/fms.2022.87
- Schoen, C. (1993). *On Hodge structures and non-representability of Chow groups*. Lemma 4.4, pp. 311–313. https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1993__88_3_285_0.pdf
- The Stacks Project Authors. *Rational equivalence*, Lemma 43.9.1, Tag 0AZI. https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AZI

### Record: agents/frobenius/E3_morphic_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit: the full morphic Abel–Jacobi obstruction

Reviewer: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), inherited effort, /root/frobenius.

This is an independent source and proof review of the proposed cycles-agent counterexample. The complete typed E.3t and E.3u in research/agents/cycles/morphic_counterexample.tex have now been independently read and pass. This includes the exact Lawson criterion, the degree-fourteen sixfold construction, the integral singular-class vanishing, the fixed elliptic family, and the geometric-generic point witness. The smooth-dominant spread formulation correctly allows auxiliary transcendental coefficients.

## 1. Exact primary sources

**[OPENED]** Walker, M. E. (2007). The morphic Abel–Jacobi map. *Compositio Mathematica, 143*, 909–944. https://doi.org/10.1112/S0010437X07002278

Full published PDF:
https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/4A44146CE680F4F3C857048FDEDD9F48/S0010437X07002278a.pdf/the-morphic-abel-jacobi-map.pdf

Exact locators independently read: Example5.5 p.928; Theorem5.7(1)–(4) p.930 and proof p.931; Corollary5.9 and its preceding factorization p.932; Theorem6.1 and Theorem6.2 pp.933–934, including the full cap-product proof; Corollary6.3 p.934; Definition3.1 pp.915–916 and Proposition3.3 p.916.

**[OPENED]** Friedlander, E. M. (2000). Relative Chow correspondences and the Griffiths group. *Annales de l'Institut Fourier, 50*(4), 1073–1098. https://doi.org/10.5802/aif.1785

Published primary PDF: https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.1785.pdf

Author primary PDF, also opened: https://dornsife.usc.edu/ericmfriedlander/wp-content/uploads/sites/233/2023/06/17.pdf

The needed published result is **Theorem3.4, p.1082**, with Definition3.1 and Theorem3.2 pp.1081–1082 and proof pp.1095–1097. Walker's citation to this paper as “4.5” does not match the published numbering: Proposition4.5 pp.1089–1090 concerns relative characteristic classes. The author copy likewise numbers the result Theorem3.4 (p.8; proof pp.18–20). We must cite the verified locator rather than reproduce the mismatch.

The effective Nagel sources and their exact numerical hypotheses were independently opened in the earlier Nori_independent_REVIEW.md. They are reused here only for the same universal relative-cohomology conclusion.

## 2. The full morphic map kills the generated relation

Example5.5 identifies the zero-cycle morphic Abel–Jacobi map on every smooth projective parameter with its Albanese map. Theorem5.7(4) gives naturality for arbitrary Chow correspondences of nonnegative dimension shift. A generator defining \(N^i(X)\) starts with an Albanese-zero zero-cycle on a smooth projective parameter and has target dimension \(\dim X-i\ge0\). Its full morphic image is therefore zero.

The theorem's printed notation reuses its index inconsistently in the displayed diagram, but both its statement and proof give the required correspondence shift. The specific zero-cycle-to-positive-dimensional-cycle application has no negative shift.

## 3. A single fixed cycle gives a nonzero elliptic family

Let \(Y\) be smooth projective of dimension \(2r+1\), and let \(\gamma\) be an \(r\)-cycle with zero rational singular class and
\[
s\gamma\ne0\quad\text{in }L_{r-1}H_{2r}(Y)_{\mathbb Q}.
\]
For an elliptic curve \(E\), put \(X=Y\times E\). The map
\[
\lambda_\gamma:H_1(E,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow
L_rH_{2r+1}(X,\mathbb Q),\qquad v\longmapsto\gamma\times v
\]
is injective. Indeed, for nonzero \(v\) choose \(w\) with nonzero intersection pairing. Capping with the pullback of \(w\) and pushing to \(Y\), exactly as in Walker's proof of Theorem6.2, gives
\[
\langle v,w\rangle\,s\gamma\ne0.
\]
The map is a morphism of inductive mixed Hodge structures; its source is pure of weight minus one. Strictness therefore gives an injection of its one-dimensional complex Hodge quotient into the target Hodge quotient.

By Definition3.1 the integral Lawson group is countable. Modulo its image, the induced homomorphism
\[
E(\mathbb C)\longrightarrow J_r^{\mathrm{mor}}(X)
\]
has countable kernel and countable preimage of the torsion subgroup: upstairs a nonzero complex linear injection can meet each integral period, or each rational multiple of such a period, at at most one point. Consequently uncountably many points give nontorsion images. This argument does not require the full morphic Jacobian to be a finite-dimensional complex torus.

Theorem5.7(4) identifies this map on points with
\[
e\longmapsto\Phi_r^{\mathrm{mor}}\bigl(\gamma\times([e]-[0])\bigr).
\]
The normalized correspondence is \(\gamma\times(\Delta_E-E\times\{0\})\), with factors ordered as parameter \(E\), then \(Y\), then target \(E\). Its total rational Betti class is zero, so its cylinder action vanishes. Yet its map to \(P^i(X)\) has nontorsion values, since the full morphic map kills \(N\).

The finite-dimensional Walker family map also vanishes: it is a homomorphism of abelian varieties whose rational \(H_1\)-map is the zero cylinder. Thus no multiplication to kill a finite Walker image is necessary for this explicit family.

## 4. Effective degree-fourteen choice

Use \(r=2\), \(Y\subset Q^6\) the degree-fourteen geometric generic hypersurface, and
\[
\gamma=(\Pi_+-\Pi_-)|_Y.
\]
The ambient primitive class is nonzero; its square has degree minus two. Its restriction has zero rational singular class by the already checked weak-Lefschetz calculation.

Friedlander's Theorem3.4 proof uses connectivity only for the characteristic-class degree
\[
u=2n-2r+2j
\]
and the final degree \(2n-2r\), and again in degree \(u\) after passing to the resolved relation space. With \(n=5,r=2,j=1\), these degrees are eight and six. Relative vanishing through degree nine is sufficient for all the required isomorphisms. The Nagel bound supplies vanishing through degree ten.

Numerically, Nagel's connectivity parameter is five, \(\mu=5\), the bundle-rank-minus-one is zero, and \(m_{Q^6}=1\). His conditions reduce to \(14\ge6\) and \(14\ge12\). The omitted parameter-bound hypothesis is also satisfied with equality.

A failure of \(s\gamma\ne0\) admits the finite algebraic witness supplied by Friedlander's Theorem3.2: a homologically trivial one-cycle on a possibly singular projective threefold and a Chow correspondence. Spread this witness over a smooth dominant parameter base above the hypersurface parameter space, retaining the homological vanishing after stratifying and shrinking. Resolve the witness and the relation space and shrink so their structural maps are smooth. Friedlander's proof then applies with the explicit Nagel connectivity and forces the ambient primitive class to vanish, a contradiction.

One must not automatically describe a witness initially given after an embedding into \(\mathbb C\) as defined over a finite extension of the geometric-generic field: its coefficients can have additional transcendence. The smooth-dominant-base formulation avoids this error; Nagel permits every smooth base. A subsequent multisection is another possible way to reduce to an étale base. The relation is finite algebraic data and its zero homology class is locally constant on a topologically trivial stratum, which is the reason the spreading step is legitimate.

## 5. Scope of the conclusion

For this construction \(X\) has dimension six, the fibres are two-cycles, and the codimension is four. The contradiction is to the universal complex family converse, integrally and rationally. The result does not assert a codimension-two counterexample or settle all lower-dimensional cases. It depends on the published Lawson-homology results with the explicit connectivity substitution, not on a conjectural identification of the full morphic object with the finite-dimensional Walker Jacobian.

## Final typed audit

The typed proof has the correct dimensions: Y has dimension five, X has dimension six, gamma has dimension two, and Z has codimension four on E times X. The homological cylinder H1(E) to H5(X) and its Poincare-dual map H1(E,Q(1)) to H7(X,Q(4)) agree with these conventions. Integral weak Lefschetz makes H4(Y,Z) isomorphic to H4(Q,Z)=Z, so equal degrees give integral, not merely rational, vanishing of gamma.

The generic-point argument for e is valid: a finite expression in N, including its Chow rational-equivalence witnesses and the relative Albanese-zero conditions, spreads on a smooth dominant base over an open of E. The image contains a nonempty complex open. The entire open would then have morphic image killed by one fixed nonzero integer, contrary to the countable torsion-preimage statement. Additional transcendental coefficients do not invalidate the argument because the base is permitted to have positive relative dimension.

For the Lawson witness, proper topological stratification (equivalently constructibility and base change for the relative homology complex) makes the zero class persist after shrinking. The model is chosen from the field generated by all finite witness coefficients, so its defining complex point is generic over the original coefficient field and is retained on these dense opens. The two resolved bases are smooth over the hypersurface parameter after generic smoothness. Thus the all-embedding formulation does not assume that an unspecified analytic exceptional locus is defined over the original countable field.

No finite-dimensionality of the full morphic target is used. The conclusion refutes the universal complex converse integrally and rationally in the stated codimension-four example.

### Record: agents/frobenius/E3_one_motivic_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit of E.3s: the large one-motivic quotient

Reviewer: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), inherited effort, /root/frobenius.

Owner file: research/agents/cycles/one_motivic_quotient.tex.

**Verdict: passed after the nonproper-parameter wording correction, now applied by the owner.**

## Primary source

Ayoub, J., & Barbieri-Viale, L. (2009). 1-motivic sheaves and the Albanese functor. *Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra, 213*(5), 809–839. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jpaa.2008.10.002

**[OPENED]** Author version arXiv:math/0607738v2, dated 21 October 2008, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0607738. The version-qualified PDF request failed; the unqualified PDF succeeded, and the abstract page confirms that v2 is current. The owner's local primary PDF and text were read independently.

Exact author locators: §1.3.1 and Lemma1.3.3 pp.16–17; Corollary1.3.5 p.18; Theorem1.3.10 pp.23–24; Proposition1.3.11 and Lemma1.3.12 pp.24–25; Remark1.3.15 p.25; Theorem3.1.4 p.49; Remark3.3.6 p.52.

The characteristic exponent inverted in §1.3.1 equals one over \(\mathbb C\); this is an integral argument.

## Proof checks

The sum of Yoneda maps indexed by actual Chow sections surjects onto the associated sheaf. Smooth quasi-projective parameters suffice because smooth affine opens cover the site. Thus no global cycle representative is assumed for an arbitrary sheafified section.

After quotienting by the images of the Serre–Albanese kernels, the result is a quotient of a coproduct of Serre–Albanese schemes. Cocompleteness and the Serre property place it in the one-motivic category. Lemma1.3.12 gives the universal property. This uses cokernels and epimorphisms, not left exactness of arbitrary colimits.

Evaluation at \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C\) is exact because étale covers of this point split. It commutes with sums, and sheafification does not change the value at the point. The kernel is therefore exactly the finite sums of images of the free-zero-cycle kernels \(K_T(\mathbb C)\), without saturation.

A smooth projective compactification \(\overline T\) sends a Serre–Albanese-zero cycle on \(T\) to a degree-zero Albanese-zero cycle on \(\overline T\). Chow localization extends the actual cycle, and refined point pullback agrees on the open. Conversely every defining generator of \(N^i(X)\) uses a proper smooth parameter. Both inclusions are integral.

The original sentence claiming factorization through ordinary \(\operatorname{CH}_0(T)\) for arbitrary nonproper \(T\) was too broad: a constant family on \(\mathbb A^1\times X\) already disproves that assertion. The owner replaced it by the correct statement for the smooth projective compactifications. The proof only uses free zero-cycles before compactifying, so no mathematical step was lost.

The component identity follows from successive left-adjoint universal properties. Theorem3.1.4 identifies the component quotient with cycles modulo algebraic equivalence; exact evaluation gives the connected-point statement. The example \(B/\mathbb Zb\) for a nontorsion point of an elliptic curve is a valid connected one-motivic sheaf which need not be an abelian variety. No finite-dimensional representability or Walker comparison is implied by E.3s.

Remark3.3.6 only anticipates a comparison with the full morphic Abel–Jacobi construction. The distinction between that construction and the finite-dimensional Walker Jacobian must be retained in subsequent revisions.

### Record: agents/frobenius/E3_walker_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent review of the integral Walker obstruction

Reviewer: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), agent /root/frobenius. Date: 19 November 2026.

## Scope and conclusion

We independently read research/agents/cycles/walker_obstruction.tex, particularly E.3j–k, and reopened the primary Ottem–Suzuki paper. The stated integral conclusion follows. No mathematical correction was identified in the reviewed argument.

## The diagonal decomposition

The complex support hypothesis on zero-cycles suffices. Choose a countable algebraically closed field of definition and embed its function field in the complex numbers. The support relation for the resulting geometric generic point involves finitely many cycles and rational functions. Spreading those data over the algebraic closure of the function field and choosing a closed point in a good open gives the relation over that algebraic closure. Finite descent and trace then give a positive integer multiple of the generic point supported on the chosen curve. Closing the relation and using localization on the first factor gives
\[
M\Delta_X=\Gamma_C+\Gamma_D,
\qquad
\operatorname{supp}\Gamma_C\subset X\times C,\quad
\operatorname{supp}\Gamma_D\subset D\times X .
\]
Universal support over arbitrary extensions is not required.

The contribution supported on \(X\times C\) lifts integrally to divisor correspondences on \(X\times\widetilde C\), after normalizing each curve component. A component dominating a curve component lifts with degree one under the normalization; a component over a singular point lifts after choosing a point of its normalization, again with degree one over the algebraically closed base. The resulting action on \(\mathrm{CH}^{n-1}(X)\) factors through \(\mathrm{CH}^0(\widetilde C)\). This group has no algebraically trivial part. Components supported at isolated points have a still simpler zero action.

For a projective resolution \(f_j:T_j\to D_j\to X\), every component supported on \(D_j\times X\) has a generically finite multisection in its inverse image. Thus it lifts after rational coefficients, including components over singular strata. Clearing the finitely many denominators gives integral \(G_j\in\mathrm{CH}^{n-1}(T_j\times X)\), with \(\dim T_j=n-1\), and the exact action
\[
M\operatorname{id}=\sum_j(G_j)_*f_j^*
\]
on algebraically trivial codimension-\((n-1)\) cycles. The degrees are correct: \(f_j^*\) produces zero-cycles on \(T_j\), and \(G_j\) has exactly the codimension needed to return codimension-\((n-1)\) cycles on \(X\).

## The integral family conclusion

Functoriality of Albanese equivalence makes this action factor through
\[
\prod_j P^{n-1}(T_j)
=\prod_j\operatorname{Alb}(T_j)(\mathbf C).
\]
For a family whose cylinder map is zero, the pullback family on \(T_j\) has zero cylinder in
\(H^{2n-3}(T_j,\mathbf Q)=H^{2\dim T_j-1}(T_j,\mathbf Q)\).
Faithfulness of the homology realization on homomorphisms of abelian varieties implies that the induced homomorphism to \(\operatorname{Alb}(T_j)\) is zero. Consequently \(M u_Z=0\).

This is sufficient integrally. For each \(a\in A(\mathbf C)\), divisibility supplies \(b\) with \(Mb=a\), and hence \(u_Z(a)=M u_Z(b)=0\). No assertion that the target \(P^{n-1}(X)\) is torsion-free is used.

## The same fourfold separates the assertions

Ottem and Suzuki, Lemma 2.4, printed author p. 4, proves \(\mathrm{CH}_0(W)=\mathbf Z\) for the threefold used in their construction. Therefore \(\mathrm{CH}_0(W\times E)\) is supported on \(\{w_0\}\times E\), by applying the equality of point classes in each fibre \(W\times\{e\}\). E.3j applies to every codimension-three abelian family on this same fourfold.

Corollary 4.2, printed author p. 10, supplies a surjective regular Walker map and a nontrivial finite kernel in the isogeny from the Walker intermediate Jacobian to the ordinary algebraic intermediate Jacobian. A point lifting a nonzero element of that kernel is ordinarily Abel–Jacobi trivial but not Albanese equivalent to zero, since regular homomorphisms annihilate the defining subgroup of Albanese equivalence. E.3g supplies an integral abelian-family parameterization of this individual point.

Thus the family-map converse holds and the proposed integral equality of point equivalence relations fails on the same fourfold. This refutes the literal integral biconditional without asserting that its family-map side fails. The rational formulation is unaffected.

## Related surface-radical calculation

We also checked the direct composition argument communicated by /root/cycles. For \(S=C^2\), let the homologically trivial modified diagonal be the degree-zero correspondence \(\gamma:S\to C\), and let \(\pi^*:C\to S\) be the transpose graph of a projection. Then \(a=\pi^*\gamma\in\operatorname{End}(S)\). For every endomorphism \(b\), the composite \(\gamma b\pi^*\) is a homologically trivial divisor correspondence on \(C\times C\), so it is zero modulo algebraic equivalence. Hence \(aba=0\), and \((ba)^2=0\); the inverse of \(1-ba\) is \(1+ba\). Thus \(a\) lies in the Jacobson radical. A fixed-point section in the fourth factor recovers \(\gamma\) from \(\gamma\times C\), so a nonzero modified-diagonal class gives a nonzero radical element. The remaining nonvanishing input is the primary Ceresa theorem, owned and audited by /root/cycles; we do not claim to have independently opened that source in this review.

## Opened primary source

Ottem, J. C., & Suzuki, F. (2020). *A pencil of Enriques surfaces with non-algebraic integral Hodge classes*. arXiv:1906.08994v2. Opened https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.08994. Checked Lemma 2.4, author p. 4; Theorem 3.1 and its construction data, author pp. 6–8; Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.2, and Remarks 4.3–4.4, author p. 10. We use the stated construction and Walker results as primary theorem inputs; this targeted review does not independently reprove their degeneration argument.

### Record: agents/frobenius/F2_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit of F.2a–b

Reviewer: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), agent /root/frobenius. Date: 19 November 2026.

We read research/sections/F_state.tex, the two supplied source files, and the current Milne and published Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin PDFs. The corrections and their proofs are sound. A minor scope clarification was suggested to the root: the elliptic curve in F.2b is over \(\mathbf C\), as required by the positive-form formulation.

## F.2a

Milne defines \(S^r\) using the generalized eigenvalue-one space of \(H^{2r}(-,\mathbf Q_\ell(r))\), printed p. 3. Theorem 1.6 on the same page instead prints \(S^{2d}(X\times X,\ell)\), while its proof explicitly uses \(H^{2d}(X\times X,\mathbf Q_\ell(d))\). The corrected sufficient hypothesis is therefore \(S^d\). We checked the independent linear-algebra argument: after extending scalars, a generalized Frobenius block \(V_a\) pairs with its Poincaré-dual reciprocal block, and the tensor is \(\operatorname{End}(V_a)\) with conjugation action. A nontrivial unipotent factor cannot act trivially by conjugation, because the centre of the full endomorphism algebra consists of scalars and a unipotent scalar is one. Partial semisimplicity at eigenvalue one thus forces every block to be semisimple.

The common-field extension powers on printed p. 2 are crossed: a \(p^{n_1}\)-Frobenius and a \(p^{n_2}\)-Frobenius satisfy \(\pi_1^{n_2N}=\pi_2^{n_1N}\) for some positive \(N\). Printed p. 4 uses uncrossed powers in the Tate-structure equivalence definition. The \(H^2(\mathbf P^1)\) test with eigenvalues \(p,p^2\) proves the incompatibility directly. Both errors also occur in the supplied TeX; they are not introduced by extraction.

## F.2b

The published Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2, and proof on pp. 1799–1801 say exactly what F.2b attributes to them. In particular Corollary 2.2 has the range \(2\le k\le n-2\), whereas the supplied early TeX prints the upper endpoint \(n\), despite correctly writing \(n-2\) in the preceding sentence.

The published proof expressly takes the closure of the convex cone of rank-one forms \(i\ell\wedge\overline\ell\) with coefficients in the CM order. The supplied proof instead infers generation of that cone from real positive generation of the vector space of one-forms. This inference is not valid without closure: a sum of positive semidefinite rank-one forms has rank one only if every nonzero summand has the same complex line, and an arbitrary line need not contain a vector with coefficients in the CM fraction field. The root's corrected approximation proof is exact. The fraction field is dense in \(\mathbf C\), simultaneous approximation and clearing denominators produce CM-order directions, and positive rescaling gives a convergent sequence of the corresponding rank-one forms. Each is the class, up to a positive real scalar, of the pullback of the origin under a homomorphism \(E^n\to E\). Closedness of the pseudoeffective cone supplies the limit.

## Opened sources

- Milne, J. S. (2007, author revision 3 November 2021). *The Tate conjecture over finite fields (AIM talk).* https://arxiv.org/pdf/0709.3040. Checked printed pp. 2–4, particularly the definition of \(S^r\), Theorem 1.6 and its proof, and the Tate-structure equivalence definition. The arXiv header retains an older upload date while the body states the 2021 revision.
- Debarre, O., Ein, L., Lazarsfeld, R., & Voisin, C. (2011). Pseudoeffective and nef classes on abelian varieties. *Compositio Mathematica, 147*, 1793–1818. https://doi.org/10.1112/S0010437X11005227. Opened full published primary PDF at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~roblaz/Reprints/Debarre.Ein.Laz.Voisin.PNAV.pdf. Checked Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2 and proof, pp. 1799–1801, and the equality of the positive-form cones at endpoint codimensions on p. 1794.
- Supplied primary source witnesses read: background/literature/milne_tate_conjecture_finite_fields/Tate2007.tex and background/literature/debarre_ein_lazarsfeld_voisin_pseudoeffective_nef/1003.3183.tex.

### Record: agents/frobenius/K0_actual_family_descent_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit: actual K0-family descent from completion

**Outcome: passed as a K0 auxiliary lemma.** Audited the complete §7 of `research/agents/real_weil/TOP_QUOTIENT_RESEARCH.md` on 2026-11-19, with primary-source checks completed at approximately 08:59 UTC. This is not a new numbered result and does not assert any Chow-group conclusion.

Let R be an excellent henselian local ring equipped with its specified coefficient field k equal to the residue field. For a qcqs R-scheme Z, the quotient of K0 of perfect complexes by differences of evaluations of actual classes on products with smooth projective connected k-curves injects integrally into the analogous quotient after completion.

The proof is correct. Excellence makes R to its completion regular. Popescu expresses that completion as a filtered colimit of smooth finitely presented R-algebras. Perfect complexes, their morphisms, and finite triangle relations descend to a single stage. In particular an equality in K0 uses finitely many generators and relations; it is not necessary to claim any inverse-limit continuity of K-theory. The residue map from that smooth stage to k lifts to R by the henselian lifting lemma. Pulling back the already descended actual complexes and relations proves the assertion. The selected coefficient field and all proper curve parameters are preserved because this is an R-algebra map.

All four cited primary sources were opened and inspected:

- Stacks Project, Theorem 16.12.1 (Tag 07GC), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07GC: regular maps between Noetherian rings are filtered colimits of smooth maps. Web reference `turn612165832view0`.
- Stacks Project, Situation 36.29.1 (Tag 09RC), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09RC: qcqs terms and affine transition maps; the adjacent Lemma 36.29.2 also supplies full faithfulness. Web reference `turn115228967view0`.
- Stacks Project, Lemma 36.29.3 (Tag 09RF), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09RF: perfect derived categories commute with the indicated limit. Statement and proof read. Web reference `turn612165832view1`.
- Stacks Project, Lemma 15.13.3 (Tag 0H74), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H74: a map from a smooth R-algebra to A/I lifts to A for a henselian pair (A,I). Statement and full proof read. Web reference `turn115228967view1`.

The limitations written by the owner are essential and accurate: this descends an already existing actual family over the completion; it does not algebraize arbitrary compatible formal K0 classes, and it does not establish a comparison with ordinary Chow equivalence.

### Record: agents/frobenius/Nori_independent_REVIEW.md

# Independent audit of C.1i: explicit counterexamples in every non-top range

Reviewer: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), agent `/root/frobenius`.
Date: 2026-11-19.
Reviewed file: `research/agents/cycles/nori_counterexamples.tex`.
Conclusion: **the proof and its numerical hypotheses are valid as written**. No change to the statement or degree choice is required. We did not modify the cycles agent's files.

## Exact primary statements opened

1. Nagel (2002), *Effective bounds for Hodge-theoretic connectivity*, author PDF <https://nagel49.perso.math.cnrs.fr/connect.pdf>, Theorem 3.13, printed p.23. Opened full PDF (`turn683175876view0`), exact theorem (`turn191802653view3`), and independently inspected the rendered primary page `research/agents/cycles/output/nagel-theorem313.png`.
2. Nagel (2004), *Lectures on Nori's connectivity theorem*, author PDF <https://nagel49.perso.math.cnrs.fr/grenoble.pdf>, Theorem 5.11 and following bibliographical paragraph, printed p.35. Opened full PDF (`turn683175876view1`) and exact theorem (`turn546446229view0`). The paragraph explicitly says that the condition that the connectivity parameter be at most n should be added to the 2002 statement. Theorem 6.2 and its proof, printed pp.36–37, were also read (`turn546446229view2`).
3. Nagel (1998), *Effective bounds for Nori's connectivity theorem*, author PDF <https://nagel49.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Nori_CRAS.pdf>, printed p.3, immediately before Theorem 2, states that the regularity constant is one for every smooth quadric (`turn546446229view1`). The same fact is Exercise 5.8 in the 2004 author version, printed p.34 (`turn546446229view0`). The 1998 announcement's sharper condition (C) is not used. Nagel2002 Remark3.14(i), printed p.26, explicitly corrects it (`turn191802653view3`).

These are primary author versions. Their printed pagination is not silently identified with journal pagination. The 2002 theorem works over the smooth-fibre open U of the projectivization of the direct sum of section spaces, exactly the parameter space used in C.1i; it applies to every smooth morphism T→U, without a dimension restriction on T.

## Parameters and inequalities

To avoid the collision between the cycle codimension and Nagel's connectivity parameter, write c for the cycle codimension and b for the latter parameter. We have

- c<n<2c;
- dim Q=2c;
- s=2c−n is a positive integer;
- r=s−1=2c−n−1<n;
- b=n, so b≤n and μ=floor((n+b)/2)=n;
- every degree is D=4c+2;
- m_Q=1.

Nagel's condition (C) is

\[
\sum_{\nu=\min(b,r)}^r d_\nu\ge m_Q+\dim Q-1.
\]

Since r<b, its left side is exactly D and its right side is 2c. Each condition (C_i), for 0≤i≤min(b−1,r)=r, is

\[
\sum_{\nu=i}^rD+(\mu-b+i)D
 = (r-i+1)D+iD=sD
 \ge1+2c+n-i.
\]

The right side is at most 4c, since n≤2c−1. The left side is at least D=4c+2. Thus every inequality has positive margin, including the hypersurface case s=1. No asymptotic choice remains.

The conclusion is relative cohomology vanishing in every degree at most n+b=2n. In the algebraic-equivalence argument, injectivity in degree 2c uses H^{2c}(Q×T,X_T)=0, and surjectivity in degree 2c after base change to the curve family uses H^{2c+1}(Q×C,X_C)=0. Since c≤n−1, both degrees lie within the asserted range. The extra degree needed for surjectivity is present.

## Finite witness, field, and trace

A relation on the geometric generic fibre is finite algebraic data. In characteristic zero, a finite definition-field extension becomes finite étale over a nonempty open of the original smooth parameter space. After further shrinking, the curve family is smooth projective, its degree-zero divisor has degree zero on every connected fibre component, and the Chow equality and any rational-equivalence witnesses hold on total spaces. Both T and the total curve space C are therefore permitted smooth bases for Nagel's theorem.

The cohomological lifting and subsequent pushforward are precisely the mechanism in Nagel2004 Theorem6.2. Proper base change for the curve projection identifies its fibre restriction. The degree-zero divisor has zero class on each fibre curve, so the class of the original ambient cycle vanishes. This is a direct contradiction argument for finite data on the specified geometric generic fibre; no assertion about fields of definition of analytic exceptional loci is needed.

For the stronger Lefschetz-image obstruction, tracing a cycle over a finite extension to the rational function field is legitimate with rational coefficients. All conjugate algebraic-equivalence relations yield the trace relation. The universal common-zero incidence is the projectivization of the kernel of a surjective evaluation map over Q. Its projective-bundle hyperplane class is pulled back from the parameter projective space and becomes zero on the generic fibre. Thus the projective-bundle formula expresses the traced generic cycle as the restriction of an ambient cycle, with the asserted codimension. This step does not assume that an arbitrary geometric generic cycle descends before taking trace.

## Quadric and homological calculations

The two displayed maximal linear spaces meet in a projective (c−1)-plane and are the two components of the indicated linear section, so their sum is h^c. The normal sequence gives self-intersection (1+(-1)^c)/2. Hence, from Z=2[Π_+]−h^c, its square has degree 2(-1)^c. The equal degrees of the two planes imply h cl(Z)=0 because H^{2c+2}(Q) is one-dimensional. The primitive class is therefore nonzero and orthogonal to every h times an ambient codimension-(c−1) class.

On the complete intersection, weak Lefschetz applies in degree 2n−2c<n. The push-pull pairing contains h^s with s≥1 and hence annihilates cl(Z); Poincaré duality gives cl(z)=0. Together with the finite-witness injectivity, this proves the nonzero Griffiths class and the stronger exclusion from L A^{c−1}_{alg}(X).

The persistence assertions use only finite-type spreading and specialization over an algebraically closed base field. A hypothetical new relation after an algebraically closed extension would specialize to one over the original algebraically closed field. They therefore apply also after adjoining the generic hyperplane and under every embedding into C.

## Scope and status

The construction covers exactly every integer pair c<n<2c, beginning at (c,n)=(2,3). In the remaining nonzero high-codimension case c=n, cycles modulo algebraic equivalence are determined by degree on a connected smooth projective variety, and a point of the smooth hyperplane has degree one. Thus the universal dichotomy stated in C.1i follows. Groups with c>n vanish. This review does not claim a positive-characteristic version of Nori's connectivity theorem.

### Record: agents/frobenius/Patel_Ravindra_open_complement_REVIEW.md

# Targeted independent review: Patel–Ravindra open-complement lemma

**Reviewer:** GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode; run RESEARCH_SA06 /root/frobenius; inherited effort setting not separately exposed.
**Date:** 19 November 2026.
**Scope:** the literal open-complement assertion in Lemma 3.2 and its displayed proof. This report does not assert that the paper's main torsion theorem is false. No numbered statement in our work uses this lemma as an input.

## Source reading

We read the complete Lemma 3.2 and proof in the primary Purdue author PDF:
https://www.math.purdue.edu/~patel471/torsionWL.pdf, author p. 7.
Theorem 2.6 and Corollary 2.7 on author p. 6 were also read, so the phrase “as above” was checked against the stated Bertini setup.

The published article is Patel and Ravindra, *Lefschetz theorems for torsion algebraic cycles in codimension 2*, Advances in Mathematics 316 (2017), 554–575, DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2017.05.018. The published lemma on p. 562 and preceding p. 561 were read as indexed primary text from the UMSL PDF. Direct full published-PDF requests timed out; no successful full published download is claimed.

The author PDF was downloaded again at 13:35 UTC by code/acquire_charzero_lifting_sources.py. Its 357911-byte SHA-256 is f10f2109386de4258593798eb9192fd3ae3c8edb68426e4e1b7d7a895b451ad1. The exact timing and successful extraction are recorded in output/charzero_lifting_sources.json.

## Explicit counterexample to the literal lemma

Over \(\mathbf C\), let
\[
Y=\mathbf P^4,\quad
X=(x_0=0),\quad
Z=(x_0=x_2=0),\quad
V=(x_0x_1-x_2x_3=0).
\]
Then \(X\) is a smooth ample hyperplane section, \(Z\simeq\mathbf P^2\subset X\), and \(V\) is an irreducible rank-four quadric cone. Its unique singular point is
\[
v=[0:0:0:0:1]\in Z.
\]
Thus \(V\) is smooth away from \(Z\), contains \(Z\), and meets \(X\) properly. The intersection \(V\cap X=(x_2x_3=0)\) is smooth away from \(Z\). These are the asserted open-complement hypotheses.

Moreover, the example is compatible with the indicated “general” Bertini degree. The ideal of \(Z\) is generated by \(x_0,x_2\), so its twist by 1 is globally generated, and Corollary 2.7 uses degree 2. A general quadric containing this plane has rank four: its quadratic form has a three-dimensional totally isotropic subspace, so rank is at most four, and the displayed example attains four. Its vertex lies on the contained plane. Therefore the degree-two example is not excluded merely by requiring a general member of that linear system.

On \(X\), the complement is the locus where both \(x_2\) and \(x_3\) are nonzero. Normalize \(x_2=1\). The remaining free coordinates give
\[
X-V\simeq\mathbf A^2\times\mathbf G_m,\qquad
H^1(X-V,\mathbf Q)\simeq\mathbf Q.
\]
Projection from \(v\) identifies \(Y-\{v\}\) with the total space of a line bundle over \(\mathbf P^3\), and \(V-\{v\}\) with its restriction over the smooth quadric \(Q\subset\mathbf P^3\). Therefore \(Y-V\) is an affine-line bundle over \(\mathbf P^3-Q\). The Gysin sequence contains
\[
0\longrightarrow H^1(\mathbf P^3-Q,\mathbf Q)
\longrightarrow H^0(Q,\mathbf Q)(-1)
\xrightarrow{\,[Q]\,}H^2(\mathbf P^3,\mathbf Q).
\]
The last map is multiplication by the nonzero degree 2, so
\[
H^1(Y-V,\mathbf Q)=0.
\]
The proposed isomorphism in degree \(1<\dim X=3\) is consequently false.

## Exact proof issue and retained limitation

The displayed sequence in the source mixes compact-supported cohomology of \((Y-X)-V\) with ordinary cohomology of the nonproper \(Y-V\) and \(X-V\). It is not the applicable localization long exact sequence for that nonproper ambient space. Artin vanishing therefore does not imply the claimed conclusion by that sequence.

This is a targeted mathematical and source check of Lemma 3.2. It is not an assessment of every possible repair to the main theorem, and it is not used to assert a counterexample to that theorem.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_SNC_Fpbar_REPORT.md

# C.3bc: rational top Chow vanishing for SNC resolutions over Fpbar

Finalized 19 November 2026 after full independent proof and primary-source audits by root and real_weil. This is a restricted theorem: existence of the indicated regular projective resolution and of a positive exceptional combination with ample negative restriction remains an explicit hypothesis.

## 1. Exact result

Let R be the strict henselization at a closed Fpbar-point of a normal local ring essentially of finite type over Fpbar, of dimension d+1, d≥1. Let Z→Spec R be regular, projective, birational, and an isomorphism away from the closed point. Let the reduced exceptional fibre E=∪E_i be SNC, and suppose D=Σa_iE_i has all a_i>0 and −D|E ample. Then restriction followed by degree is an isomorphism CH^d(Z)_Q→Q^{number of components}; CH^d(Z−E)_Q=0. Consequently its ordinary quotient B^d is also zero rationally.

The proof does not identify algebraic equivalence conventions, does not lift proper families from a reducible exceptional fibre, does not compare K with KH, and does not assert resolution in arbitrary dimension. It gives no integral vanishing or extension to an algebraically closed field transcendental over Fp.

## 2. Proof and the exact source-scope correction

On a smooth m-dimensional stratum, Levine's rational comparison identifies the Adams weight w of K_n with CH^w(−,n). We use the published Theorem3.1, pp276–278. Above w=m+n there are no degree-n cycles. At w=m+n every degree-n cycle is a point of the cube over a k-point of the stratum; proper pushforward therefore gives a surjection from the direct sum of CH^n(k,n). Totaro's Theorem1, p181 identifies these field groups with Milnor K_n(k), which is torsion over Fpbar for n>0. Smooth projective CH0_Q is Q by degree, using curves through pairs of points and torsion of their Jacobian points.

For a union V=A∪B of SNC components, Geisser–Hesselholt TheoremC, printed p30 gives excision for the closed-union Milnor square after inverting p. Thomason–Trobaugh Theorem8.1, p367 patches it on finite affine covers. The resulting connecting map preserves the ordinary Adams weight, with no support or Thom shift. The precise source is the paragraph BEFORE Levine's Lemma2.1 on p258, which explicitly describes Grayson's construction for arbitrary schemes, iterated homotopy fibres, and delooping. The statement of Lemma2.1 itself has a regular-ambient hypothesis; we use only the elementary generalized-eigenspace module argument in its proof on p259. The final fragment states this distinction explicitly. Parent and peer freshly inspected that page.

An induction on dimension and component number then proves K_0(E)_Q^(d)=⊕CH0(E_i)_Q=Q^c. In the induction the predecessor K_{n+1}(A∩B) has exactly top weight (m−1)+(n+1), so it vanishes; this is the critical index calculation.

KST TheoremA and equation(1.6), author pp2–3, supply a finite detecting thickening for K0(Z). The constant-group kernel system has inclusion transition maps, so its being pro-zero implies an actual finite zero kernel. GH TheoremA, p29 and finite affine descent identify that thickening rationally with E. Smooth pointed-étale model descent and Fulton's rational Chern ring comparison, Example15.2.16(b), pp294–295, then inject CH^d(Z)_Q into Q^c.

For an ample H on E, take the exceptional curves C_j=H^{d−1}[E_j]. Their component-degree matrix M is symmetric, has nonnegative off-diagonal entries, and satisfies Ma<0. Conjugating by diag(a) makes every row sum negative, and the exact quadratic identity proves negative definiteness. Thus these exceptional curves span every component-degree vector. Localization kills all of CH^d(Z)_Q on the puncture.

## 3. Independent checks and execution record

The real_weil full independent proof/source PASS is timestamped 12:06:00.083550UTC; its detailed review is research/agents/real_weil/C3bc_SNC_Fpbar_top_independent_REVIEW.md. Parent's preliminary targeted check was received before the tool clock12:07:00UTC; its final full certification is timestamped12:12:36.242839UTC. Parent also read the separate energy lemma, its program and entire JSON without claiming a rerun. The energy lemma is not needed for this shorter component-degree proof.

The mathematical text compiled by four LuaLaTeX/BibTeX passes starting 12:05:46.712431UTC, runtime3.346874491s, four pages146550bytes. After final filename promotion and the explicit bibliography-scope correction, the final-path build started12:13:15.416834UTC and took3.016476542s, producing four pages146904bytes. Every return code was zero and there were no warnings or over/underfull boxes. The executable builder and exact current output are code/build_SNC_Fpbar.py, output/C3_SNC_Fpbar_build.out and output/C3_SNC_Fpbar_build.json. No bounded numerical calculation is being substituted for this proof. Parent's final source certification is recorded at12:12:36.242839UTC in notes/ROOT_C3bc_SNC_FPBAR_AUDIT.md.

The primary-source acquisition script code/acquire_SNC_top_sources.py and output/acquire_SNC_top_sources.json retain original start times, durations, sizes and SHA256 hashes. The published Levine PDF is 5491369bytes, SHA256 5f4de92e51f03dfb9a4708f70ed9a8f58d2c2a51e310eeb4d597be84c7450984; the Totaro PDF is773722bytes, SHA256 3447b12c9108d37528d998376051d7e60f0461584f61c1e980bdaa46ada43aee. Actual acquisition durations were99.769088048s and9.008752825s, concurrently, not estimated. Images of Levine's printed pp258 and276 were inspected.

## 4. Focused literature comparison and remaining research

We opened Binda–Krishna, Zero-cycle groups on algebraic varieties, current arXiv2104.07968v2 (11January2022), Theorem1.6 and Corollary1.7, author pp4–5. These compare normal-crossing Levine–Weibel Chow groups and motivic cohomology, and construct refined restrictions after the specified coefficient changes. We do not replace their current statement by the broader wording of the earlier version. They are neighboring results, not an asserted proof of our strict-local theorem.

We also opened Burke–Popa–Shen, Negative K-theory and Hodge theory (15September2026), Theorem9.1, pp28–31, and Lemma13.1, p40. The former concerns complex projective isolated klt threefolds, with stated Bloch-conjectural rational-singularity and additional LCI refinements; the latter concerns algebraic semilocal models and compactifications. Neither supplies invariance under henselization/completion or a positive-characteristic SNC family-lifting theorem. The separate SNC research note records their exact limitations.

These searches support no originality or priority claim. The next main question is whether rational alteration or ldh methods can replace the assumed resolution. A generically finite alteration is not an abstract blow-up that is an isomorphism off the closed point, so the KST constant-group finite-detection argument cannot simply be reused. A low-dimensional resolution corollary needs a precise existence theorem and an actual positive exceptional combination with ample negative restriction.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_lowdim_Fpbar_REPORT.md

# C.3bd: isolated surface and threefold germs over an algebraic closure of a finite field

## Final statement and scope

The final proof is `C3_lowdim_Fpbar_top.tex`. Let R be the strict henselization at a closed Fpbar-point of a normal local ring essentially of finite type over Fpbar. If 2 <= dim R <= 3 and the punctured spectrum X is regular, then CH^(dim R - 1)(X) with rational coefficients is zero. Consequently its ordinary quotient by algebraic equivalence is zero. The puncture condition is automatic in dimension two and remains an explicit hypothesis in dimension three. Every positive characteristic is included.

This is a restricted corollary of C.3bc. It does not assert resolution in higher dimension, integral torsion bounds, vanishing over transcendental extensions of Fpbar, or vanishing for a threefold germ with a singular puncture. It is not recorded as a reset of the main research gate. We make no priority claim.

## Exact construction

We first apply Cossart–Piltant Theorem 1.1 to the affine scheme Spec R. Its affine-projectivity clause and its regular-locus clause provide the initial regular projective resolution simultaneously. Kollár–Witaszek's desired ample exceptional divisor is then constructed on a further modification without invoking another unspecified projective resolution.

More precisely, write L2 for the coherent rank-one sheaf occurring in Kollár–Witaszek Lemma 8. On the initial regular resolution, its torsion-free pullback M embeds in the invertible reflexive hull M**. Thus J = M tensor (M**) inverse is an ideal, equal to the unit ideal on the puncture and at all codimension-one points. In dimension three Cossart–Piltant Proposition 4.4 principalizes this ideal by blowups in regular centres in its nonprincipal locus. In dimension two its support consists of finitely many closed regular points, and Stacks Lemma 54.4.1 gives the corresponding point blowups. These constructions preserve regularity, projectivity, and the entire punctured open. The resulting invertible quotient of the pulled-back L2 defines the required map to Kollár–Witaszek's second Proj. Lemma 8 now applies directly.

We next embedded-resolve the entire reduced closed fibre, whose dimension is at most two, using Cossart–Jannsen–Saito Corollary 0.4. This precise choice avoids an additional identification between a named exceptional locus and the full closed fibre. Kollár–Witaszek Lemma 6 and relative ampleness restore an ample exceptional divisor after this step.

Finally normal Hartogs identifies the global sections of a sufficiently positive power of the exceptional divisor sheaf with an ideal I of R. Global generation gives I O_Z = O_Z(nF), inside the common rational function field, so -nF is effective. If I were the unit ideal, the trivial line bundle would be relatively ample, making the birational projective morphism finite and hence an isomorphism over normal R. In the singular case this is impossible. Thus I is m-primary, and -nF has strictly positive coefficient along every component of the full closed fibre. All hypotheses of C.3bc are now verified.

## Material correction in the audit

The first draft inferred simultaneous projectivity and preservation of the regular puncture from separate resolution statements. That inference was not justified: Kollár–Witaszek's convention does not require a resolution to be an isomorphism over the regular locus, and the general projectivization assertion in BMP+ does not preserve the SNC open automatically. Root identified this source-scope gap before checkpoint13. The earlier peer endorsement was explicitly withdrawn on that step.

The final proof replaces the inference by the explicit principalization construction above. The exact new primary inputs are Cossart–Piltant Proposition 4.4, current author version p. 141, and Stacks Lemma 54.4.1, Tag 0AHH. The revised complete peer review passed at 12:31:59 UTC. Root freshly read the same inputs and the revised proof, recorded final PASS at 12:35:36 UTC in notes/ROOT_C3bd_LOWDIM_FPBAR_AUDIT.md, and authorized finalization after checkpoint13 was saved. The earlier endorsement is not represented as certification of the corrected proof.

## Primary-source record

- Cossart and Piltant (2019), current arXiv v2 dated 8 January 2019: Theorem 1.1, author pp. 3–4, and Proposition 4.4 with proof, author p. 141. The downloaded source and its hash are retained. We use the theorem and do not claim an independent verification of the full resolution algorithm.
- Kollár and Witaszek (2026), complete four-page arXiv author version dated 5 February 2021: Lemmas 6 and 8, pp. 2–3, and surrounding construction. Publisher metadata records online publication in January 2024 and issue publication in July 2026. The publisher PDF retrieval returned HTTP 429; all proof locators here explicitly refer to the opened author version.
- Cossart, Jannsen, and Saito (2013), current 169-page author v2: Corollary 0.4 and its proof, p. 5. This is the author-version numbering, not an invented locator in the later book.
- Stacks Project Proposition 28.27.13(7), Tag 01Q3; Remark 31.17.2, Tag 0BCS; and Lemma 54.4.1, Tag 0AHH. Complete statements and relevant proofs were opened and read.
- BMP+ current v3, Proposition 2.14 and Remark 2.15, were checked as neighboring scope; they are not cited as supplying the missing preservation assertion.

The full bibliography includes opened markers and these limitations. Acquisition scripts, timed outputs, SHA-256 hashes, the standalone wrapper, and compilation script are retained alongside the proof.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_smooth_exceptional_REPORT.md

# C.3az: smooth exceptional divisor in positive characteristic

## Status and exact scope

The final complete proof is in `C3_smooth_exceptional_top.tex`. Root and real_weil independently read the complete proof and exact primary inputs and passed it; real_weil completed at 11:38:43.203963 UTC, and both receipts were present at the 11:39:52 UTC tool-clock reading. The canonical result row is now registered. The hypotheses are an algebraizable strictly henselian normal local ring of characteristic p, a regular projective modification that is an isomorphism on the puncture, a single smooth connected exceptional Cartier divisor E, and ample conormal L. The result applies in every positive characteristic and every dimension d+1 >= 2. No cone retraction is assumed.

The conclusion is stronger than the ordinary-quotient vanishing alone: refined restriction gives CH^d(Z)_Q ≅ CH_0(E)_Q; Chow localization then gives CH^d(X)_Q ≅ CH_0(E)_Q/(c1(L) CH_1(E)_Q). The ordinary quotient on Z is Q by restricted degree, and that on the puncture X vanishes.

## New step, with the uniform exponent made explicit

The previously audited KST/GH argument supplies injectivity, without any retraction. The new argument constructs actual families. Through any two points of E, successive ample sections cut a smooth projective curve C, and lifted sections cut a regular projective surface W. Properness over a local base forces global regularity once regularity is known along the closed fibre.

For every proper smooth parameter curve P and line bundle F on C×P, the obstruction at the nth infinitesimal step is H²(C×P,L_C^n⊠O_P) = H¹(C,L_C^n)⊗H¹(P,O_P). Choose n0 so that the first factor vanishes for every n>=n0. The finitely many earlier additive obstructions are killed by taking pth tensor powers; after at most n0−1 such operations, the same exponent p^e works over the entire parameter curve and for all later infinitesimal levels. This does not use an unbounded sequence of p-powers.

The ideals defining C and the closed fibre are cofinal. Projective formal existence algebraizes the compatible family over the completed base. Popescu descends that actual line bundle to a smooth algebra over R; henselian smooth lifting supplies a map back to R with the same residue point. Hence the result is a line bundle on the actual fixed product W×P, with precisely F^(p^e) on C×P.

Take P=C and the normalized diagonal line bundle. Proper pushforward of its two fibre Chern classes supplies an ordinary algebraic relation on Z restricting to p^e([x]−[o]). After rationalization every degree-zero class lifts. An exceptional curve has restriction −c1(L)[D] of nonzero degree, which supplies the remaining degree, proves the top Chow isomorphism, and kills the open ordinary quotient.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_surface_reduction_Fpbar_REPORT.md

# C.3be — arbitrary excellent local domains with residue Fpbar

## Certified conclusion and exact scope

**Proved.** Let R be an excellent local domain of dimension N at least two with residue field isomorphic to the algebraic closure of Fp. Then CH_1(Spec R) with rational coefficients is zero. The puncture, equipped with the inherited dimension function delta(p)=dim(R/p), consequently has CH^(N−1) with rational coefficients zero.

The ambient domain need not be normal or henselian. Its puncture need not be regular. No coefficient field, equal-characteristic hypothesis, algebraization over a field, or resolution in dimension greater than two is used. In particular the assertion includes mixed-characteristic domains. Ordinary B is a quotient and vanishes wherever that quotient has been defined; the text does not impose a product-family definition over a nonexistent coefficient field on a mixed-characteristic ring.

This is a residue-field-specific positive result. It does not close the unrestricted rational top-quotient question over arbitrary algebraically closed fields, and it is not counted as resetting the scheduled main-gate movement clock. No integral vanishing, finite torsion group, or common annihilating exponent is asserted.

Final proof: C3_surface_reduction_Fpbar.tex. The previous draft file is now a pointer to the final file.

## Complete proof structure

1. **Surface geometry with all required properties at once.** An excellent normal local surface is regular outside its closed point. Stacks/Lipman 54.14.5 and the normalized-point construction 54.6.5 resolve it by normalized closed-point blowups over that point. Excellence makes each normalization finite. A further sequence of point blowups from 54.15.6 makes the whole reduced closed fibre SNC. These constructions preserve the puncture. Starting with the closed-point blowup also covers an already regular surface.

   The exceptional divisor of an ordinary blowup is effective Cartier, with its negative tautological bundle relatively ample. Finite dominant normalization preserves effectivity, the Cartier property, and relative ampleness. A sufficiently weighted sum of the preceding total transform and the next exceptional divisor is negative ample for the composite. The first divisor's total transform retains the whole closed-fibre support. This simultaneously gives a projective regular model, preserved puncture, SNC fibre E, and D=sum a_i E_i with all a_i positive and −D relatively ample. It does not use the invalid conjunction of separate resolution and projectivization existence assertions identified in the earlier C.3bd audit.

2. **One finite K0 detecting level.** KST Theorem A and (1.6) give the exact pro sequence for the closed point and the resolution. Since K0 of the local ring and of all its Artinian quotients is Z, quotienting by the diagonal graph makes the restriction from the constant K0(Z) a monomorphism of pro-groups. Its level kernels form a descending system of subgroup inclusions. Pro-zero therefore forces an actual zero kernel at one finite level.

   At every infinitesimal closed fibre E_b, p^b=0, even in mixed characteristic. The reduction E inside E_b is nilpotent. GH Theorem A applies to rings in which p is nilpotent, not only to Fp-algebras. Finite affine-cover K-theory descent gives K0(E_b)_Q=K0(E)_Q. Hence K0(Z)_Q injects into K0(E)_Q. No nilpotence assumption on the ambient ring or on Z enters.

3. **Determinant, with the order of operations explicit.** A multidegree-zero line bundle on the SNC curve E is torsion: component Jacobian points descend to finite fields, and the remaining node-gluing scalars lie in the torsion group k*. For a line bundle L on Z, first choose M with L^M|E actually trivial. K0 injectivity makes [L^M]−[O_Z] a torsion K0 class. Projectivity over an affine base supplies the resolution property, so vector-bundle K0 equals perfect K0 and the vector-bundle determinant is available. Applying it to an integer annihilating this K0 class makes L torsion. Thus Pic(Z)_Q injects into the multidegree space Q^c.

4. **An explicit intersection argument.** The exceptional degree matrix M is symmetric with nonnegative off-diagonal entries, and Ma has strictly negative coordinates. For Q=diag(a)Mdiag(a) and b_i its row sums,
   x^tQx=sum b_i x_i^2−sum_(i<j) Q_ij(x_i−x_j)^2.
   This proves negative definiteness and invertibility. The exceptional line bundles span all multidegrees and therefore Pic(Z)_Q. Cartier-divisor closure on regular Z makes Pic(Z)→Pic(U) surjective, while those exceptional bundles restrict trivially. This proves Pic(U)_Q=CH_1(Spec B)_Q=0 for the normal local surface.

5. **Every curve comes from a surface, without henselianity.** Catenarity puts a curve prime p in a two-dimensional prime quotient B=R/q. Its finite normalization T is a normal integral semilocal ring; every maximal residue field is still Fpbar. Each maximal localization has dimension at most two. In dimension two, Steps 1–4 give torsion of its class group, with no henselian hypothesis; in lower dimensions it is a field or DVR. For any fixed Weil divisor on T, a common positive multiple is therefore Cartier at every maximal ideal, hence Cartier everywhere by the rank-one reflexive-sheaf description. Every invertible module over a semilocal ring is free. This common multiple is thus principal and Cl(T)_Q=0. The finite pullback of the dimension function has generic value two, so Cl(T)=CH_1(T). A prime above p/q is a height-one prime, and finite pushforward sends its class to a positive finite residue-degree multiple of [V(p)]. The surface result therefore kills every generator of CH_1(Spec R)_Q. Localization at the omitted closed point loses no dimension-one cycle. No assertion about equality of all maximal heights in T is needed.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C3_uniform_gysin_REPORT.md

# C.3t: explicit nonzero ordinary Gysin images

The owned LaTeX fragment C3_uniform_gysin.tex proves a non-torsion ordinary algebraic Gysin image for every r>=2 and r+1<=N<=2r-1. The endpoint N=2r-1 is exactly the proposed low-degree critical equality i=(N-1)/2, so the construction extends the earlier three-dimensional example to every odd critical dimension.

We use the Segre cones from C.3s and a smooth incidence divisor with explicitly specified linear sections. Its base is a smooth weighted Fermat hypersurface; inside it, an explicit smooth plane Fermat curve contains both the generic point witness and the fixed comparison point. Thus the ordinary algebraic equivalence comes from an actual flat curve family and needs no Bertini or abstract local-Picard family identification. The proper pushforward has coefficient1. C.3e preserves the nonzero quotient class in the strict-local puncture.

The construction depends on the already audited C.3e and C.3s. It introduces no new literature theorem and no claim of priority. The main limitation is exact: for m=r-1 the base of the incidence becomes zero-dimensional and this family argument no longer applies. Characteristic zero is part of the statement, and nothing here asserts that its transcendental-point witness remains non-torsion over Fpbar.

Both the root and cycles have independently audited the complete typed proof and passed it. Cycles has been asked, with the root's authorization, to integrate the fragment after C.3s. The script and output are mathematical certificates of the explicit algebraic identities in a finite grid; the uniform argument and non-torsion are proved in the fragment itself.
