### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_genus5_integral_lattice_REPORT.md

# Genus-five Prym construction: the complete integral Hom obstruction

**Status:** proved conditional construction exclusion, not a counterexample to Question2. This report is reconstructed after the 2026-11-19 10:14 UTC scratch reset. The original exact calculation ran at 09:37:18.986283 UTC (0.013099318s); the reconstructed program has a separate measured runtime. Cycles and parent independently checked the full lattice argument before recovery. Cycles' audit was conditional on the stated geometric premise, not a fresh source check.

## 1. Geometric premise and exact conclusion

Let A be a complex abelian surface with End(A)=Z and a primitive polarization of type (1,2). The genus-five construction considered here starts with a genus-three curve D and its elliptic quotient, with the complementary abelian surface of type (1,2), and an étale double cover F→D obtained from a degree-two principally polarized isogeny B→A. We assume the principally polarized Prym of F/D is the indicated B, with the compatible lattice markings described below. This is the precise Prym premise in the Clingher–Malmendier–Shaska construction, not an assumption that every conceivable genus-five map has this shape.

Under this premise, **every actual composite A→J(F)→A is even**. More precisely the ideal of all such integer scalars is either 4Z or 2Z, depending on the marking. All 720 possible symplectic mod-two markings give 4Z in 672 cases and 2Z in 48 cases. Thus this particular family of full-span genus-five curves does not remove the residual factor two, even if arbitrary integral homomorphisms through its Jacobian are allowed. This conclusion is stronger than computing only the class of the displayed curve, but does not constrain arbitrary Jacobians.

The primary source is Clingher, Malmendier, and Shaska, *Geometry of Prym varieties for certain bielliptic curves of genus three and five* (7 September 2021 author version), <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.04839v2>. The complete PDF was opened; diagram(1.3) p3 and Theorem1.2 p5 were read. Its letters differ from ours. The ramified-Prym quotient convention must not be confused with the principally polarized étale Prym used below. The proof below is an independent integral lattice computation under that exact premise.

## 2. The genus-three lattice

Write Λ=H₁(A,Z)=Z(e₁,f₁,e₂,f₂), with alternating polarization form

`E_L=diag(J,2J)`, where `J=[[0,1],[-1,0]]`.

Its dual lattice is `Λ#=Z(e₁,f₁,e₂/2,f₂/2)`. Let u,v be a symplectic elliptic basis. On the rational decomposition `H₁(J(D),Q)=H₁(A,Q)⊕H₁(E,Q)`, the principal form is `2E_L⊕2J`. An integral symplectic basis is

`a₁=(e₁+u)/2, b₁=v, a₂=(f₁−v)/2, b₂=−e₁, a₃=e₂/2, b₃=f₂/2`.

Direct pairing gives one in each pair and zero between distinct pairs. The projection J(D)→A acts as multiplication by two on the A coordinate. The duality calculation uses this principal form; it does not treat the nonprincipal E_L as a unimodular form.

Choose the degree-two principally polarized cover B→A with lattice `Λ_B=Z(2e₁,f₁,e₂,f₂)`. The restricted form E_L/2 is principal on this lattice. All changes of its symplectic marking are represented by

`P=diag(2,1,1,1) G`, with `G∈Sp₄(Z)`.

Write P_j for its columns. The character of the cover detects the e₁ coordinate; on J(D), it is nontrivial on a₁ and trivial on the remaining displayed symplectic basis vectors.

## 3. The genus-five lattice

Use the rational decomposition `H₁(J(F),Q)=H₁(A,Q)⊕H₁(B,Q)⊕H₁(E,Q)`, identifying the B vector space with that of A via its isogeny. The principal polarization form is

`4E_L ⊕ E_L ⊕ 4J`.

An integral lattice is generated by

`A₁=(e₁/2,0,u/2), B₁=(0,0,v/2)`,

`a₂±=(f₁/4, ±P₁/2, −v/4), b₂±=(−e₁/2, ±P₂/2,0)`,

`a₃±=(e₂/4, ±P₃/2,0), b₃±=(f₂/4, ±P₄/2,0)`.

This is the standard integral transfer/difference lattice of the étale double cover with the chosen character, glued to its marked principally polarized Prym. In particular the factor two in the transfer and the factor four in the invariant form are retained. Omitting either factor changes the answer incorrectly.

Since A is simple and End(A)=Z, its rational homomorphisms to either A-vector-space factor are scalar and its homomorphisms to E vanish. Therefore every rational A→J(F) is `(a,b,0)` and every rational J(F)→A is `(c,d,0)`.

## 4. All incoming integral maps

Testing an incoming map against the dual lattice under the principal form amounts to testing `(4a,b)` against the E_L-dual conditions. The resulting necessary and sufficient form is

`(a,b)=(x/2,y)`, with x,y integers satisfying

`x+yG₂₁=0 (mod2)`, and `yG₂j=0 (mod2)` for j=2,3,4.

These conditions are not merely necessary for a convenient pair of maps: they describe the full integral Hom lattice. The use of the principal dual lattice is essential; testing only the visible A projection would miss the half-integral incoming coordinate.

## 5. All outgoing integral maps

Testing every displayed lattice generator shows that an outgoing integral map has the form `(c,d)=(2u,v)` for integers u,v with

`u f₁+vP₁=0`, `vP₂=0`, `u e₂+vP₃=0`, `u f₂+vP₄=0` modulo2.

The first factor two follows already from A₁. The remaining congruences arise from the four plus/minus pairs. Again this is the full integral Hom lattice. The composite of an incoming and an outgoing map is the scalar

`xu+yv`.

## 6. Parity and the exact ideals

If v is even, the outgoing equations force u even, so the composite is even. If v is odd, the equations force u odd and imply that the second row of G is `(1,0,0,0)` modulo2. The incoming equations then force x≡y, so `xu+yv≡x+y=0`.

If row₂(G) differs from `(1,0,0,0)`, the incoming conditions force both x and y even; the outgoing conditions force both u and v even. Each lattice is precisely 2Z², so the scalar ideal is 4Z.

If row₂(G) equals `(1,0,0,0)`, incoming `(x,y)=(1,1)` is allowed. Outgoing `(u,v)=(2,0)` is always allowed, giving the scalar two. The parity proof gives the reverse divisibility, so the ideal is exactly 2Z. We do **not** need to claim that the row condition guarantees an outgoing vector with v odd; that stronger assertion is unnecessary and was deliberately not used.

The full mod-two symplectic group has 720 elements. Exactly 48 have the indicated second row, giving the 48/672 split. The program enumerates all matrices by their four columns, tests every symplectic pairing, constructs both inverse-image lattices from their mod-two residues together with 2Z², and computes the gcd of all pairwise scalar products of generators. This is an exact finite certificate of the stated gluing calculation. The arbitrary-marking proof above is independent of the enumeration.

## 7. What remains

The remaining surface question is still whether the integral numerical cycle P²/2 exists on A×Â, equivalently whether A is an actual direct summand of some product of Jacobians. Excluding this one genus-five Prym construction does not exclude higher-genus Jacobians or other families of integral curves. It must not be counted as closing or narrowing that universal existence statement without an additional theorem that every candidate factors through this construction; no such theorem is asserted.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_lagrangian_divisor_obstruction_REPORT.md

# Exact obstruction for Lagrangian-surface divisor pushforwards

Status: **proved method exclusion; no main-gate movement and no priority claim**.

We prove that every divisor on each of two proposed full-span Lagrangian surfaces has an even mixed Matsusaka coefficient after mapping to `A × A^dual`, when `A` is a generic type-(1,2) surface with `End(A)=Z`. This checks all divisor classes, not merely the fundamental surface class or the restrictions of ambient divisors.

The decisive property is that the surface's Albanese variety admits an odd-degree isogeny from a power of `A`. On `A^n`, every integral curve homomorphism is `lambda_d S`, with `S` a symmetric integral matrix. A homomorphism to `A × A^dual` has rows `(r, lambda s)`, and its mixed curve coefficient is `2 r S s^t`. Finite-flat pullback along an odd-degree isogeny preserves the parity obstruction. Albanese factorization handles every divisor curve on the surface.

The full proof is `C4_lagrangian_divisor_obstruction.tex`. It is intentionally unnumbered and separate from the integrated main results. The parent may assign a label if it is useful in the final methods discussion; it should not be counted as a resolution of the remaining surface case.

## Opened primary sources

* Bastianelli, Pirola, and Stoppino, *Galois closure and Lagrangian varieties*, author version v2 (14 June 2010), <https://arxiv.org/pdf/0912.3377>. We opened the complete primary PDF and read Theorem 6.8, author pp. 25–26, including the Albanese-lattice proof. It identifies the Albanese variety of their LG surface with the square of the associated type-(1,2) surface. The publication is Advances in Mathematics 225(6), 3463–3501 (2010), DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2010.06.006. No assertion here relies on their Proposition 7.6 or on a claim that the surface's Neron–Severi group is generated by ambient divisors.
* Grossi and Moretti, *An explicit class of Lagrangian surfaces*, author version v1 (18 February 2025), <https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13087v1>. We opened the full primary HTML and read Proposition 4.2, Theorem 5.6, Proposition 6.2, and Corollary 6.3. Their associated type-(1,2) surface is `A_0/G`, with `|G|=3`, and the quotient surface has Albanese variety `(A_0 × A_0)/diag K`, with `K=(Z/3)^2`. The two are related by odd-degree isogenies. Publisher metadata gives International Journal of Mathematics 37(10), article 2650052 (2026), DOI 10.1142/S0129167X26500527; the mathematical locators used here refer to the opened author version, not to an independently read published PDF.

## Independent check

The cycles agent independently checked the full algebraic argument and its treatment of arbitrary surface divisors. In particular, that audit confirmed the direction of the isogeny, the factor of two in the mixed block, the odd-degree pullback argument, and the absence of any ambient-NS-generation hypothesis.

## Remaining gate

The argument controls only curves obtained from varieties whose Albanese is odd-isogenous to a power of the original surface. It does not control all curves spanning `A × A^dual`. The exact integral numerical Poincare-cycle criterion remains unchanged. Likewise no consequence for arbitrary supersingular threefolds in characteristics two or three is asserted.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_ordinary_real_multiplication_REPORT.md

# C.4w: ordinary full real multiplication, including characteristic two

The canonical Serre–Tate lift transfers C.4v to ordinary abelian varieties in every positive characteristic. ### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_positive_characteristic_RM_REPORT.md

# C.4x — full real multiplication in positive characteristic

The original Yu 2003 paper gives a direct argument in positive characteristic. No canonical lift, supersingular realization, or ordinary hypothesis is needed.

## Exact proved scope

For a dimension-g abelian variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, with a full degree-g totally real integer-ring action and a compatible polarization, the polarization Euler-characteristic gcd is a p-power. Under the intrinsic equality of Lie-module and regular-module classes in the Grothendieck group, that gcd is one. Total ramification of p forces the equality because the coefficient algebra is local Artinian with a unique simple module and both modules have length g.

Combining with the previously proved actual-factorization bounds gives s_J dividing 2's p-part for surfaces and 6's p-part for threefolds. The Lie condition removes the remaining characteristic-prime factor. No failure statement is inferred if the condition fails.

## Independent verification

The complete typed proof passed independent checks by both `/root/cycles` and `/root`. The parent additionally opened the complete published primary source, checked the multiple-prime reduction and visually inspected the decisive pages. Their audit receipts were logged at the tool-clock time 2026-11-19 07:45:14 UTC. The owner of the C section confirmed integration after C.4w at 07:47 UTC.

## Opened primary source and exact locators

Yu, C.-F. (2003). On reduction of Hilbert-Blumenthal varieties. Annales de l'Institut Fourier, 53(7), 2105–2154. https://doi.org/10.5802/aif.2002

Full published PDF: https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_2003__53_7_2105_0.pdf

- Section 1.6, p. 2111: the compatible polarization module. We retain an explicit compatible-polarization assumption, so we need no further existence theorem from the cited Rapoport source.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_real_multiplication_REPORT.md

# C.4v: full real multiplication

We prove a new affirmative family rather than merely a reformulation of the residual gate. For a characteristic-zero abelian variety of dimension g with the full ring of integers of a totally real degree-g field acting and fixed by the Rosati involution of a polarization, the gcd of Euler characteristics of line bundles is one. Therefore all such surfaces and threefolds are actual direct summands of products of Jacobians by C.4j.

The proof is an integral trace-lattice argument. The homology is projective of rank two over the full integer ring. Its balanced integral alternating forms form an invertible codifferent-valued determinant module. A local generator supplies a perfect pairing at any chosen rational prime; its residue lifts globally, and a large positive multiple of that prime times an existing polarization supplies positivity without changing perfection. All balanced forms have Hodge type (1,1), as shown explicitly on the real two-plane decomposition. The prime may be two; no inversion of two is hidden.

The same result includes simple varieties whose full endomorphism ring is the maximal order of a CM field, using the unique positive involution. This exact input was freshly opened in Milne's primary notes, Proposition1.39/Corollary1.40pp20–21. Appell–Humbert and the positivity theorem were freshly opened in the proof of Proposition6.1pp46–47. No priority claim is made.

Root and cycles completed full typed proof and source reviews and approved integration. It also includes a good-reduction consequence, justified by extending each of the finitely many required line bundles to the regular abelian scheme and preserving Euler characteristic. The generic End=Z type(1,2) surface and the nonmaximal obstruction-prime cases remain untreated.

# Residual C4 research through the 09:50 review, with recovery notes

This is a reconstruction of the post-checkpoint09 report following the 10:14 UTC scratch reset. Original source readings and proof checks are retained as historical events; downloads and computations were rerun with separate actual timings.

## Main gate remains unresolved

For a surface A, C.4r identifies actual splitting from a product of Jacobians with an integral numerical representative of P²/2 on A×Â. For a threefold the analogous class is P⁴/24. The generic End(A)=Z, type(1,2) surface and arbitrary supersingular threefolds in characteristics two and three were not settled by the leads below. No method exclusion in this report is counted as main-gate movement.

## Genus-five full-span Prym curves

The complete integral Hom calculation is in `C4_genus5_integral_lattice_REPORT.md`. It allows every incoming and outgoing integral homomorphism through the indicated Jacobian, not only the maps originally displayed by the geometry. Conditional on the exact Prym premise, every composite is even, with ideal4Z for672 and2Z for48 of the720 symplectic mod-two markings. Parent and cycles independently checked this proof. Cycles' check was conditional on the geometric premise, not a fresh reopening of the primary geometry.

Primary: Clingher, Malmendier, and Shaska, *Geometry of Prym varieties for certain bielliptic curves of genus three and five*, arXiv2005.04839v2,7September2021. Complete primary PDF opened, diagram(1.3)p3 and Theorem1.2p5 read. The ramified-Prym quotient convention is not confused with the principally polarized étale Prym.

## October2026 supersingular derived-isogeny theorem

An Jiang, Zhiyuan Li, and Ziwei Lu, *Derived equivalences and isogenies of supersingular abelian varieties*, arXiv2610.24666v1,17October2026. Complete primary PDF downloaded and read. Definition1.1 allows twists and chains. Theorem1.2 and its proof in §3 pp5–6 show derived isogeny for all supersingular abelian varieties of the same dimension; the construction uses twisted Fourier–Mukai equivalences. It does not give an actual untwisted product decomposition or a prime-to-p factorization of the identity.

Theorem4.1 pp6–7 gives, in every characteristic and dimension g>2, supersingular examples A such that Aⁿ is never isomorphic to Âⁿ. The proof uses A=Eᵍ/H with an alpha_p subgroup defined by F_{p²}-linearly independent coefficients. An assumed isomorphism would produce an endomorphism of E^{gn} of degree p^{2n} whose kernel contains ker(F^{gn}), forcing p^{gn}|p^{2n}. This contradiction shows that principal polarizability of arbitrary supersingular threefolds is not a valid shortcut. It still does not obstruct being a direct summand of a larger product of Jacobians.

## EGFS monodromy scope

Engel–de Gaay Fortman–Schreieder, arXiv2507.15704v3, was reopened, including Theorem1.6. Its specified matroidal-family criterion uses independent boundary monodromy logarithms proportional to rank-one quadratic forms. In the family A×Â obtained by varying A, H¹ contains two isomorphic copies of the same variation, so every corresponding monodromy logarithm has even rank. Thus this precise criterion cannot simply be applied to that correlated subfamily. The very-general principally polarized fourfold theorem also does not specialize automatically to the three-dimensional type(1,2) product locus. No extension of the theorem was proved.

## New Chern-method exclusion after09:50

`C4_semihomogeneous_obstruction.tex` proves that all semihomogeneous Chern constructions miss P²/2 and have even mixed degree-three coefficients. The proof uses the full general semihomogeneous Chern identity, not just rank-two examples. It also covers Chern classes of the familiar odd-rank virtual Fourier transform of a universal one-point ideal sheaf, by its exact K₀ decomposition. Arbitrary moduli kernels and arbitrary algebraic cycles are outside its scope.

## Exact current Fourier/motive literature limitations

Li–Zou's author primary text, <https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~hzou/papers/derivedab/>, was opened completely. Corollary1.2.2 relates derived isogenies to motive isomorphisms; §3.1 explicitly uses Chow correspondences with Q coefficients, and equation(3.1.1) is ch(P) in CH*(X×Y)_Q. The integral twisted Mukai lattice in §3.2 is a different realization. Neither the rational-motive theorem nor integrality of that cohomological realization supplies an integral numerical P²/2 cycle.

Hasan–Hassan–Lin–Manivel–McBeath–Moonen (2025), *Integral aspects of Fourier duality for abelian varieties*, DOI10.1007/s00229-025-01662-7, was opened at the complete publisher HTML. Theorem4.5 and §1.2 construct integral transforms lifting (2g+d)! times the classical transform; Theorem5.5 works after inverting (2g+d+1)!. This is a precise integral denominator theorem, but it does not remove the prime two in the residual surface problem. The statements and coefficient rings were checked; no claim that their full proof was independently rederived is made.

## Reproducibility

Fresh acquisition records, URLs, SHA256 hashes and times are in `output/residual_and_K2_sources_manifest.json`. The reconstructed genus-five script reproduces the720-marking result in a separately measured run. The original 09:37 run and the fresh 10:20 run are distinguished. No reconstructed artifact claims to be a byte-identical copy of a lost file.

# Further residual checks, 19 November 2026

Tool clock during these checks: 08:35:53 UTC. These are source and method checks, not a new closure of the type-(1,2) surface or supersingular-threefold cases. No new result number is assigned.

## Supersingular cycles: kernel information is not saturation

We opened Oliver Gregory's complete published HTML, *Torsion codimension 2 cycles on supersingular abelian varieties*, Canadian Mathematical Bulletin 66(2) (2023), 458–466, DOI 10.4153/S0008439522000431, at <https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/canadian-mathematical-bulletin/article/torsion-codimension-2-cycles-on-supersingular-abelian-varieties/9FA8E4E719B07441E78F9FF936C6FDC2>.

Theorems 1.1 and 4.1(1) prove that torsion codimension-two cycles on a supersingular abelian variety over any algebraically closed field of positive characteristic are algebraically trivial. Theorem 4.1(2) proves integral equality of homological and algebraic equivalence in codimension two over the algebraic closure of a finite field. These are precise results about the kernel of the cycle class map. They do not assert saturation of its image in the integral crystalline lattice. In §2 the displayed crystalline comparison explicitly tensors with `K=W(k)[1/p]`. Thus that comparison does not eliminate the remaining characteristic-prime coefficient in C.4u. We read the proof strategy in §4, including its use of a denominator-cleared diagonal decomposition and divisibility for the torsion Abel–Jacobi cokernel; this divisibility argument does not apply to the finite-index numerical cycle lattice in C.4r.

## Prym schemes in characteristic two

We independently opened the full 52-page author PDF of Achter and Casalaina-Martin, *Putting the P back in Prym*, dated 18 December 2024, at <https://www.math.colostate.edu/~achter/math/prym1224.pdf>. Theorem A (author p. 2), Theorem 5.12, Theorem 6.4 (author p. 46), and Lemma 5.17 (author pp. 44–45) retain characteristic two and the finite separable-cover hypotheses. The odd exponent-three case is an étale noncyclic degree-three cover of a genus-two curve and produces a **principally polarized two-dimensional** Prym. It is not an existence theorem for the generic nonprincipally polarized type-(1,2) surface or an arbitrary supersingular threefold. Theorem 5.3 and the relative Theorem 6.1 use numerical curve equivalence, consistent with the Matsusaka method already used in C.4. We do not infer a new existence result from their all-characteristic comparison theorem.

## Recent Weil-fourfold theorem

We opened the complete 24-page author PDF of Floccari and Fu, *The Hodge conjecture for Weil fourfolds with discriminant 1 via singular OG6-varieties*, at <https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~lfu/articles/HCWeilViaOG6.pdf>. Published metadata: Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées 210 (2026), article 103876, DOI 10.1016/j.matpur.2026.103876. Theorems 1.1–1.3, author pp. 2–3, give rational Hodge algebraicity and an isogeny description. Theorem 1.5, author p. 4, is explicitly formulated with rational l-adic coefficients. The footnote on author p. 5 states that the argument needs the Kuga–Satake construction only up to isogeny. These assertions do not supply an integral divided Poincare class on the residual product. We checked exact scope, not every proof in this paper. Its singular-locus/double-cover geometry remains a possible source of new cycles, but no odd mixed coefficient has been constructed from it here.

## Integral Tate counterexamples in characteristic zero

We opened the full primary HTML of J. S. Milne, *On the integral Tate conjecture for abelian varieties*, arXiv:2509.06707v1 (8 September 2025), at <https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06707v1>. Its unnumbered theorem transfers a failure of integral Hodge over C to a failure of integral Tate after a finite extension of a field finitely generated over Q. The field has characteristic zero. It neither proves a failure for the particular product of a type-(1,2) surface with its dual nor supplies a positive-characteristic counterexample by specialization. The distinction is retained.

## Other search leads not used as theorems

A primary arXiv abstract for Huang–Jiang–Yang, *Degree of irrationality of abelian surfaces*, arXiv:2609.02169, states a classification of the surfaces admitting a degree-three rational map to the plane. We did not audit its full proof or use this as a new manuscript theorem. A degree-three rational map alone does not furnish an odd scalar factorization through Jacobians. The explicitly associated Lagrangian Galois-closure construction is already covered by the all-divisor parity lemma in the separate report.

The remaining main cases are unchanged. This conclusion means that these particular checks did not resolve them; it is not a claim that their status in the entire literature has been proved open.

### Record: agents/frobenius/C4_residual_literature_2026_REPORT.md

# Residual C.4 investigation: source checks and unsuccessful routes

Date: 2026-11-19. This report records further work after C.4x. It contains no new claim that Question 2 is settled for a generic endomorphism-ring-Z type-(1,2) surface or for an arbitrary supersingular threefold in characteristics 2 and 3. No new numbered theorem or completion row is created for these searches.

## 1. Precise remaining objects

The main surface test remains a complex abelian surface A with End(A)=Z and primitive Neron–Severi generator of type (1,2). The exact ordinary integral numerical Poincare-cycle criterion of C.4r remains decisive. The calculation for cycles supported in proper abelian-subvariety translates in C.4q only treats that subgroup. The non-Jacobian result C.4t for the principal polarizations of A×Ahat does not exclude signed minimal cycles or a direct summand in a larger product of Jacobians.

For supersingular threefolds, C.4u reduces the obstruction to the characteristic prime and the universal bound reduces its exponent to one: only 2 or 3 can remain in characteristics 2 or 3, respectively. C.4x disposes of real multiplication examples satisfying its full action and Lie-module hypotheses; no such action has been supplied on an arbitrary supersingular threefold.

## 2. Kahn 2026: the latest version distinguishes the required comparison explicitly

Opened the complete current HTML of Bruno Kahn, *Divided powers on abelian varieties*, arXiv:2602.11135v2, submitted 8 June 2026 (internal date 5 June). URL: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11135v2 . The earlier author PDF https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~bruno.kahn/preprints/div-ab01.pdf is the first version dated February 2026; it is not silently used as the current version.

Exact checks:

- Proposition 1.1 proves weak divided powers in **etale Chow groups**, away from the characteristic.
- Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.3 give the canonical structure and Fourier transform in the stated etale quotient, with the precise treatment of 2-torsion.
- The introduction, under “Algebraic and etale cohomology classes,” and Question 1.11 explicitly distinguish ordinary algebraic classes from etale classes. Their rational equality and the saturation of the latter do not identify the two integral lattices.
- Proposition B.6 identifies the torsion cokernel of the ordinary one-cycle class map as a quotient, with divisible kernel, of H^{g−3}(X,H^g_et(Q_l/Z_l(g−1))). Question B.7 asks for control of multiplication maps on this group. This is an obstruction formulation, not a proof of its vanishing on A×Ahat.
- Theorem 1.10 has been corrected in v2. Its relative statement is restricted to the appropriate eigenspaces for symmetric line bundles and inverts M!p, with M=min(2g,cd(S)+2). The blanket relative assertion of v1 is explicitly withdrawn by the author. We use neither the withdrawn assertion nor a relative ordinary Chow assertion.

Opened references: turn968976604view1; turn561926606view0–3. The relevant statements and surrounding text were read, not merely their abstracts. No independent verification of the whole new preprint is claimed. In particular, existence of an etale class P^3/3! on a fourfold does not finish C.4.

## 3. Hasan–Hassan–Lin–Manivel–McBeath–Moonen 2025

Opened the full published article *Integral aspects of Fourier duality for abelian varieties*, manuscripta mathematica 176, article 64 (25 August 2025), https://doi.org/10.1007/s00229-025-01662-7 .

Theorem 4.5 constructs a transform lifting (2g+d)! times the usual one. Theorem 5.5 gives the Fourier identities and Beauville decomposition after passing to Z[1/(2g+d+1)!]; the polarization-dependent sl2 statement additionally inverts the polarization degree parameter. The positive-characteristic hypotheses in Section 3.2 are retained. These results control denominators but invert the very small primes at issue here. They therefore supply no missing odd surface class or characteristic-2/3 supersingular class.

Opened references: turn537918067view2; turn598248693view2–3. This is a source-scope check, not a new obstruction theorem.

## 4. Why the literal matroidal-family theorem is not immediately applicable

Opened the latest full Engel–de Gaay Fortman–Schreieder version, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.15704v3 . The relevant hypotheses are in Definition 4.1 and Theorem 4.10; the monodromy formalism is in Section 2.5, especially Definition 2.12 and Lemma 2.13.

Their matroidal family has nonzero rank-one monodromy logarithms around the distinguished independent boundary components. For a family of abelian varieties of the form A×Ahat, a relative polarization identifies H1(A,Q) and H1(Ahat,Q) as rational local systems. Thus every monodromy logarithm on the product is a direct sum of two conjugate operators and has rank twice the rank of the operator on A. This persists under isogeny and finite base change. Consequently a nonzero rank-one logarithm cannot occur in such an isotypic family.

This elementary rank observation shows that the literal matroidal-family hypothesis cannot simply be asserted for the residual surface family. It does **not** rule out adaptations to grouped rank-two degenerations, and does **not** imply algebraicity or nonalgebraicity of the desired cycle. The very-general ppav conclusion also does not specialize in either direction to this special locus.

Opened references: turn864092994view0; turn763967464view3; turn681223935view0. The later Engel–Schreieder 2026 degree paper and the sixfold optimality paper were already checked in the C.4x report; their hypotheses do not erase this distinction.

## 5. Supersingular polarizations and the small-Mumford–Tate lifting route

Opened Oort, *Newton polygons and formal groups: Conjectures by Manin and Grothendieck*, Annals of Mathematics 152(1) (2000), 183–206, complete published PDF at https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/oort.pdf . Remark 6.4, pp. 204–205, records a three-dimensional supersingular component in the moduli of dimension-three varieties with polarization degree p^6, for every prime p. The paper later writes p^3 once for that degree; we retain the initial moduli convention and do not propagate this inconsistent exponent.

The comparison source https://webspace.science.uu.nl/~oort0109/OortFinalEdited.pdf was also opened. Theorem 7.5(3), author p. 28, states dimension floor(g^2/4) for the principally polarized supersingular locus, and Remarks 7.6 and 8.6 explain failures of this behavior without principal polarizations. These sources prevent treating principal or prime-to-characteristic polarizability of arbitrary supersingular threefolds as automatic. They do not by themselves resolve the Jacobian-summand problem. The original references Katsura–Oort (1987), Remark 6.10, and Oda–Oort (1978), Corollary 3.4, were identified from Oort's bibliography but have not been marked as independently opened in this continuation.

Opened Lam–Oswal, *Lifts of supersingular abelian varieties with small Mumford–Tate groups*, complete author version arXiv:2208.07809v1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.07809 . Theorem 1.2(2), p. 2, lifts supersingular threefolds over Fpbar to varieties isogenous to a product of elliptic curves. Remark 1.3 specifies Witt-vector liftings; Section 1.6, p. 3, assumes p odd throughout. Proposition 2.1 makes the filtered Dieudonne isogeny formulation explicit. Publisher metadata for the later IMRN 2024 paper was located, but the full publisher text failed to load; the theorem locators and odd-characteristic restriction here refer explicitly to the opened author version.

The lift does not produce an actual product or a retraction of prime-to-p degree. No opened primary result upgraded an arbitrary integral gluing of elliptic factors into a Jacobian-product summand. We therefore do not use the lift to remove the residual p-primary factor. The theorem does not cover p=2 in the opened version.

## 6. Odd Prym–Tyurin and secant-sheaf leads

Opened Lange–Recillas–Rojas, *A family of Prym–Tyurin varieties of exponent 3*, complete author version https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0412103 . The actual Theorem 5.2 on author p. 13 identifies the constructed principally polarized varieties as products of two trigonal Jacobians. The introduction on p. 2 misnumbers this as Theorem 5.3; the actual Lemma 5.3 is a representation identity. We checked the theorem and its proof on pp. 13–17, as well as Corollary 6.4 on p. 20. An odd Prym–Tyurin realization there would be useful, but is not supplied by this source. Opened references: turn945148879view0 and turn141016688view0–1.

# C.4u: supersingular threefolds away from characteristics two and three

The full proof is in C4_supersingular_addition.tex. ### Record: notes/ROOT_ALL_CHARACTERISTIC_PICARD_RESEARCH.md

# Uniform ordinary-quartic construction after review 9

Research lead proposed after review 9; not a registered theorem at this writing. The certified C.3bf remains in its exact characteristic-five, N≥4 scope. Frobenius is preparing a separate complete extension, provisionally C.3bg; cycles independently checked the ordinary-quartic and canonical-cup calculations below. This note does not itself change a main status.

## An explicit ordinary open set in every characteristic

For any prime p, put F0=xyz(x+y+z). This is the union of four projective lines with six distinct transverse nodes in every characteristic. Its dual graph is K4. The normalization exact sequence identifies H¹(O_C0) with the three-dimensional graph cokernel k^6/(k^4/k); semilinear Frobenius is bijective because the incidence matrix has entries in Fp.

There is also a direct coefficient calculation. In the standard H²(P²,O(-4)) basis indexed by a1=(2,1,1), a2=(1,2,1), a3=(1,1,2), the plane-quartic Hasse–Witt entry is the coefficient of x^(p a−b) in F^(p−1). For F0, factor

    F0^(p−1)=(xyz)^(p−1)(x+y+z)^(p−1).

Each diagonal coefficient becomes the coefficient of one pure monomial of degree p−1, hence equals one. Every off-diagonal coefficient has one exponent −1 after the factor is removed, hence equals zero. Thus the Hasse–Witt matrix at this singular quartic is I3 for every prime. The formula itself follows from the plane-curve exact sequence and the Cech representatives, so it does not presuppose smoothness at this test point.

Let t_m run through fifteen algebraically independent coefficients, one for each degree-four monomial, and set F=F0+sum(t_m m). The Hasse–Witt determinant is a polynomial in these coefficients with value one at zero, and is therefore nonzero at the generic point. The nonempty smooth open in the full quartic linear system meets this ordinary open. Thus the specified geometric generic quartic is smooth and ordinary in every characteristic. Its coefficient of z^4 is nonzero, so z0,z1 restrict to a basepoint-free canonical pencil when that pencil is needed for N=3.

## Producing the nonsplit first neighborhood

For any smooth plane quartic C, its canonical system is O_C(1). The Euler sequence and Serre duality show H¹(T_P²|C)=0: the map H¹(O_C)→H¹(O_C(1))^3 is dual to the basis map k^3→H⁰(K_C), hence is an isomorphism. The normal sequence then makes

    H⁰(C,O_C(4)) → H¹(C,T_C)

surjective. The canonical multiplication Sym²H⁰(K_C)→H⁰(K_C²) is an isomorphism: both spaces are the six-dimensional quadrics on the canonical plane curve, which has no quadratic equation. Serre duality therefore lets the normal displacement H realize any symmetric cup form on H⁰(K_C). A nondegenerate form exists also in characteristic two. Choosing an independent generic quartic H gives a nondegenerate form.

Over k=Fp(t_m,s_m)^alg, with the s_m the independent coefficients of H, the complete polynomial data F,H,ell and F+t ell H thus specify the same nonsplit Segre construction as C.3bf. The extension-class image is the span of the three selected projective coordinates for m≥2. The cited first-order obstruction formula works in every characteristic; no characteristic-zero logarithm is used.

## The dimension-three endpoint

For m=1, take ell=x0 z0+x1 z1. Its zero divisor over C is the projective bundle of the line kernel of O_C²→K_C, hence is C itself, and L_H=K_C². The target has no vector part. The source extension has rank two. Pullback by ordinary Verschiebung again splits it. The map from its kernel (Z/p)^3 to the two-dimensional vector group has k-span of dimension two, and therefore its Fp-image has dimension at least two. The safe subgroup conclusion is an injected (Z/p)^2; k-linear rank two alone does not prove its finite image has exactly that order.

One can construct each actual family on a smooth proper curve in J^(p) through zero and the chosen kernel preimage, using the composed Picard map. This avoids requiring that the whole lifted J^(p) embed in the extension. The same first-order Poincare obstruction, higher coherent vanishing, proper formal existence, prescribed-first-jet approximation, and endpoint detection then need to be checked in the full proof.

No conclusion about a nonzero higher Chow product follows from this divisor kernel. The nonsplit conormal connecting-map obstruction described in the owner's higher-restriction research note remains a separate issue. No priority is claimed.

# Root full audit: C.3az

**PASS.** AI-produced by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode). We read the entire four-page typed argument and independently rederived each step. ## Scope retained

The base is the strict henselization at a closed k-point of a normal local ring essentially of finite type over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0. The dimension is d+1, with d>=1. A projective birational modification is regular and is an isomorphism away from the closed point. Its reduced exceptional fibre E is a single smooth connected Cartier divisor, and O_E(-E) is ample. These are genuine restrictions. There is no retraction from the modification Z to E. The theorem proves CH^d(Z)_Q ≅ CH_0(E)_Q, the exact quotient formula on the puncture, and B^d(Z)_Q ≅ Q with B^d(X)_Q=0 for actual ordinary algebraic equivalence.

## Independent derivation

1. Abstract blow-up pro-descent and K_0 of local rings give a monomorphism from the constant K_0(Z) pro-object to the infinitesimal exceptional fibres. Its kernel terms form a decreasing system of inclusions. A pro-zero such system has a zero term, so one finite stage detects K_0(Z). Nil-relative K-theory in characteristic p becomes zero after inverting p; finite affine Mayer–Vietoris descent gives injectivity into K_0(E)[1/p]. No uniform p-exponent over infinitely many infinitesimal stages is used.
2. The algebraizable strict-local hypothesis permits finite pointed-etale smooth models for Z. Regularity and properness over the local base allow removal of the image of any nonsmooth locus away from the marked point. The natural rational Chern-character ring isomorphism passes to the filtered limit and commutes with the Cartier pullback. This yields the required injective codimension-d Chow map.
3. A sufficiently ample complete-intersection curve C in E can be chosen smooth and connected through any prescribed points x,o. Relative Serre vanishing lifts its cutting sections to Z. Independence of the restricted differentials makes their common zero scheme W regular of dimension two along C. Any nonempty closed bad locus in the proper scheme W has image containing the closed point of the local base, which contradicts this regularity. The same properness argument excludes additional components. The induced conormal on C remains ample.
4. For an entire line bundle F on C×P, where P is a smooth connected projective parameter curve, the obstruction to the successive square-zero lift is H^1(C,L_C^n) tensor H^1(P,O_P). Serre vanishing kills every such group after one fixed index n_0. At the finitely many earlier indices, tensoring by p kills the additive obstruction. We can take the fixed total exponent p^(n_0−1) for the whole family. The preceding restrictions are raised together at each step; this gives a compatible formal system, rather than unrelated pointwise lifts or an unbounded sequence of powers.
5. The C-adic and closed-fibre-adic ideals have the same radical on the noetherian proper surface, hence cofinal powers. Projective Grothendieck existence over the completion algebraizes the line bundle. Algebraizing its inverse and their pairing verifies actual invertibility. Excellence makes completion a regular map. Popescu gives a smooth finite-stage algebra carrying the bundle. The residue-field point of that smooth algebra lifts to the henselian ring. Pullback gives an actual bundle on the fixed product W×P with the prescribed entire closed-fibre family. Preserving the residue-field map preserves that family, not merely its numerical class.
6. For P=C and the diagonal line bundle, the two fibre classes push from W to Z. Tor-independent Cartier base change sends their difference to p^e([x]−[o]) on E. Thus all degree-zero zero-cycles on E lift rationally to actual ordinary algebraically trivial classes on Z. Injectivity then identifies the exact ordinary kernel of the restricted degree map.
7. An exceptional curve D has restricted self-intersection −c_1(L)[D] of nonzero degree. It supplies the missing degree direction, proving surjectivity of the full Chow map. Localization gives the quotient by c_1(L)CH_1(E). The same boundary class spans B^d(Z)_Q and restricts to zero, proving B^d(X)_Q=0.

### Record: notes/ROOT_FINITE_JET_FAMILY_RESEARCH.md

# Finite jets, fixed bundles, and the remaining actual-family problem

Root research, 19 November 2026, after checkpoint 14. This records an attempted route to the unrestricted characteristic-zero rational top quotient. It does not change a numbered theorem or the movement ledger.

Let E be a projective exceptional variety, L an ample conormal line bundle on E, and C a fixed smooth projective parameter curve over the coefficient field. If a vector bundle F0 on E×C is fixed, relative Serre vanishing for the projection to C gives

    H²(E×C, End(F0) ⊗ pr_E*L^n) = 0

for all sufficiently large n: all positive higher direct images vanish, and C has coherent cohomological dimension one. This removes the high-order deformation obstructions for that fixed restriction. The bound depends on F0. Moreover, pr_E*L is not ample on the entire product, so it would be incorrect to infer vanishing of every positive cohomology group on E×C; H¹ coming from C can remain.

The unresolved step is to represent the desired relative K0 classes by a compatible family with a fixed mod-E object and a controlled bound. An equality of vector-bundle classes in K0(E×C) does not imply a stable isomorphism of the bundles: exact-sequence relations need not split on a projective scheme. Finite detection of an endpoint class, or eventual constancy in a particular Adams weight, therefore does not by itself supply the compatible objects to which Grothendieck existence could be applied. We have not established that stronger representability statement. The already proved descent from an existing completed actual family remains available, but does not construct that family.

### Record: notes/ROOT_FINITE_THICKENING_BOUNDARY_RESEARCH.md

# Finite detection along a principal centre: exact remaining boundary issue

Root research, 19 November 2026, 12:58–13:01 UTC. This is a method analysis, not a new registered theorem for the remaining ordinary restriction gate.

Suppose a regular projective modification f:Z→Spec R is an isomorphism outside the closed point of a local domain R. For any nonzero h in its maximal ideal, the enlarged centre V(h) also makes an abstract blowup square: the modification is already an isomorphism away from this centre. KST Theorem A and exact sequence (1.6), freshly opened in the root C.3be audit, apply to its h-adic thickenings. K_0(R)=K_0(R/h^b)=Z, so the same diagonal-graph quotient and descending-kernel argument prove that K_0(Z) injects into K_0(Z×_R R/h^b) at some actual finite level b. In characteristic p, the finite thickening to the full divisor Z_h has p-primary nil-relative K-groups by GH Theorem A. Thus one obtains rational injectivity into K_0(Z_h). This is a full-divisor assertion, not an assertion about its punctured open part.

Let X be the puncture and Y=X∩V(h), and suppose an actual class alpha on X restricts to zero on Y. A K_0 lift z on Z need not vanish on Z_h. Its restriction lies in the kernel of restriction from the whole divisor to its punctured part, hence in perfect K-theory with support at the exceptional part. Finite detection cannot be applied to declare z zero. To deduce the desired punctured restriction injectivity one would have to prove that this supported class is the restriction of an exceptional-boundary class on Z, with a controlled nonzero integer multiplier. That is the additional step.

The whole divisor Z_h can be singular. Its supported perfect K_0 cannot silently be replaced by G_0 of the reduced exceptional fibre. Coherent exceptional sheaves have derived Tor contributions under restriction, and the Cartan map K_0→G_0 on a singular scheme can have a kernel. In the SNC calculation, even the degree-unit edge terms are subject to the weighted negative-ample intersection identity; a preserved dual-complex loop alone supplies no surviving obstruction. The source and target of the missing boundary lift must therefore remain explicit.

The real_weil agent independently confirmed this diagnosis on 19 November 2026 and is testing whether codimension and depth yield an actual range theorem. No such theorem or counterexample has been established here. Termwise rational nilinvariance also does not identify an inverse limit of integral K_0 groups, tensored afterward with Q, with the inverse limit of their rationalizations; it provides no uniform denominator across infinitely many thickenings.

The root additionally read the complete current owner note `agents/frobenius/C3_SNC_top_RESEARCH.md` and its entire weighted energy proof. The product E=(cycle of rational curves)×P^1 cannot simply be placed with ample conormal in a regular threefold while keeping its proposed top torus class: the self-intersection/Cartan relation contradicts that proposed survival. The explicitly opened Kollár2014 primary paper gives the relevant plumbing and isolated-contraction construction, but its subsequent small resolutions alter the component restriction map. We do not count this as a new counterexample.

## Exact correspondence-image gate

C.1n was checked using the full arbitrary-source and correspondence-degree quantifiers in manuscript14:46. A numerically trivial but homologically nonzero source cycle defines a nonzero cohomological functional to an ample target class while acting as zero on algebraic cycles. Thus the criterion implies standard D on all source varieties. The zero correspondence also forces the target Griffiths group to vanish. Conversely, under D on all products, realization of whole numerical motives is faithful; Jannsen's Theorem1 supplies an image projector and hence an algebraic preimage modulo numerical equivalence. Vanishing of the target Griffiths group upgrades it to algebraic equivalence. This is the exact fixed-target gate, with endpoint codimensions reducing to D alone. The proof does not assume algebraic Kunneth projectors. The same argument works for a fixed Weil cohomology over an algebraically closed base field. # Unresolved characteristic-zero top quotient: current research record

Date: 19 November 2026, 10:45--10:50 UTC. This note records an unsuccessful route and source checks, not a new theorem or a smaller main gate.

## Test case and exact missing step

Let V be a smooth quintic surface over Qbar, extended to C, with L=O_V(1)=K_V. Its positive twists have H1(V,L^j)=0; H2(V,L)=C and H2(V,L^j)=0 for j>=2. The first absolute infinitesimal K2 term has the candidate component H2(V,L) tensor Omega^1_(C/Q). A local transverse-curve residue can see scalar multiples of db. This alone does not determine the ordinary algebraic-equivalence quotient.

The missing question is the image of actual families on a fixed product X times Q, where Q is a proper smooth parameter curve. In particular, a possible H2(V,L) tensor H0(Q,Omega^1_Q) contribution cannot be discarded merely because q(V)=0. The product-of-curves proof C.3ar uses actual Picard deformations in H1(V,L^j) and therefore does not cover this example.

We considered presenting an ordinary family through a correspondence on a nonhomogeneous Cartier surface and its relative Jacobian. Its constant abelian part might constrain the desired component, but neither the required vanishing nor a construction attaining it has been proved. Generic absence of an isotrivial curve family is not assumed. Formal deformation classes are not silently substituted for actual fixed-product families.

Searches included “Srinivas local Chow groups algebraic equivalence cone surface absolute differentials quintic”, “Chow group punctured spectrum henselian local ring algebraic equivalence top cycles characteristic zero”, exact phrases “local Chow groups” with “algebraic equivalence”, and “henselian” with “algebraic equivalence” and “cone”. - Cortinas, Haesemeyer, Walker, and Weibel, *K-theory of cones of smooth varieties*, arXiv:0905.4642v2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/0905.4642: full primary PDF opened. ### Milne normalization checks

Theorem1.6 in both the supplied and current PDF prints S^(2d)(X×X,ell), while its proof uses the generalized eigenvalue-one space in H^(2d)(X×X,Qell(d)). With the source's definition of S^r, the hypothesis needed is **S^d(X×X,ell)**. The corrected claim has the following elementary proof. Over a splitting field, let V_a be a generalized a-eigenspace of Frobenius on H^r(X). Poincaré duality identifies the corresponding reciprocal block with V_a^*. Their tensor is End(V_a), and Frobenius acts by conjugation. If a nontrivial unipotent Jordan factor U occurred, conjugation by U would be a nontrivial unipotent operator on End(V_a): an operator commuting with every endomorphism is scalar, and a scalar unipotent operator is the identity. The hypothesis S^d makes that conjugation the identity, a contradiction. Hence every block is semisimple. We do not treat the printed top-degree hypothesis as an unconditional proof of general Frobenius semisimplicity.

The definition of equivalence of a p^(n1)-structure pi1 and a p^(n2)-structure pi2 on printedp4 uses pi1^(n1 N)=pi2^(n2 N). Base change requires the crossed powers **pi1^(n2 N)=pi2^(n1 N)**, as the preceding Frobenius discussion on printedp2 correctly states. For example, H²(P¹) over Fp has pi1=p; over Fp² it has pi2=p². The crossed equality holds, whereas the printed uncrossed equality would require p^N=p^(4N), impossible for N>0. No power-change argument here uses the uncrossed formula.

### Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin version checks

The supplied early Corollary2.2 prints 2≤k≤n. Its preceding argument and the published Corollary2.2 have the correct range **2≤k≤n−2**. At k=n−1 and k=n the claimed strict cone difference does not occur. The early proof of Theorem2.1 also phrases a claim about nonnegative combinations of CM-lattice one-forms too strongly for the subsequent rank-one forms. The published proof correctly takes the **closure** of the convex cone of rank-one forms arising from CM-lattice directions. To check the step directly, the fraction field of the CM order is dense in C; approximate each coefficient of a one-form by elements of that field, clear their common denominators, and rescale the rank-one forms by the positive square of that denominator. Their limits give every rank-one positive form. Pullback of the origin along the corresponding map E^n→E supplies the algebraic divisor; closedness gives the asserted pseudoeffective limit. Thus the published result is supported without the faulty early finite-combination wording.

- C.3i–j: reopened Kollár (2016), *Maps between local Picard groups*, https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2016-4/2016-4-022.pdf, Theorem1.7(i) p463, §2.5 p466, Definition3.3 pp467–468, §3.5 p469, and Example4.2 pp469–470. The full local Picard identity component is not the subgroup defined by ordinary Chow algebraic equivalence. The latter is covered by images of proper Picard varieties after descending each family to one algebraic neighbourhood and extending its line bundle to a smooth projective compactification. Its intersection with a characteristic-zero unipotent restriction kernel is trivial. The explicit cone example still has kernel (C,+)^3 after quotienting by ordinary algebraic equivalence. ### Record: agents/cycles/all_degree_local_REPORT.md

# C.3af: ordinary local restriction in every codimension

Finalized, independently passed by root and frobenius, and integrated after C.3ae. For every r≥2 and N≥4^(r−1)+2r−1, the specified product-K3 construction gives an integral ordinary restriction cokernel surjecting onto Pic⁰(C)(C), where C is the Fermat plane quartic. Hence the ordinary rational J^r map is not surjective in this entire range. The first thresholds are N=7 for r=2, N=21 for r=3, and N=71 for r=4.

The Bastianelli-Pirola-Stoppino Galois-closure surface is the residual fibre product over a rational ruled surface. The chosen quartic is explicitly Hodge-generic among smooth quartics containing the fixed line. Over (mathbf Q(i)), the two character twists of the standard orthogonal representation are absolutely irreducible and conjugate. Hence (T\otimes H^1(E)) is simple over (mathbf Q), has a nonzero ((3,0))-part, and contributes no level-one summand. The argument consequently controls every source parameter curve, not merely a fixed family.

We checked the quartic Jacobian-ring duality and the degree-three to degree-four multiplication. Its joint image is all degree four, so the common kernel is exactly the hyperplane line. The class (	au) has nonzero primitive image and square (-36). The three-column rank condition is nonempty, witnessed by (s_i=wz_i), and is defined over the chosen countable coefficient field. Its simultaneous intersection with the transverse-base-locus open is therefore legitimate for the 36 algebraically independent coefficients.

The rational Chern-character lift and rank-one conormal wedge obstruction are those already checked in C.3ae. The selected Künneth component receives only the stated primitive divisor factor. The Hodge lemma reduces it to a one-dimensional primitive Néron–Severi factor, and the rank-three map kills it. \]

We rederived the missing-factor argument. The odd degree lies on \(C\). Each K3 factor must contribute total cohomological degree four after multiplication by its \(\tau_\nu\). A degree-four input already vanishes; a degree-zero input must receive an \(H_\nu\) from the indicated power of \(a\), which gives \(\tau_\nu H_\nu=0\) after integration. There is at least one such missing input in both terms. A \(K_C\) insertion kills the curve's degree-one component. Thus the boundary map kills every mixed class, not only algebraic classes. The resulting Picard family has zero differential and is constant, integrally.

The field argument is consequently legitimate. It is applied only to cycles on the smooth projective exceptional section \(H\). A Hilbert component containing a complex point is the base change of a component over the algebraically closed countable field; a point over that field exists. A chain of proper curves, normalized, and the universal flat family show ordinary algebraic equivalence to a cycle over that field. The boundary's image is therefore contained in \(\operatorname{Pic}(C)(\overline K)\). No finite-type parameterization of cycles on the strict-local puncture is assumed.

Localization and self-intersection then define \(\rho\) on all target Chow classes modulo the stated Picard subgroup. Its compatibility with parameter fibres follows by using the same closure on the fixed proper model times the parameter. The quotient is uniquely divisible: division is inherited from complex Jacobian points, and a point whose nonzero multiple is defined over the algebraically closed \(\overline K\) is itself defined there, since multiplication is finite.

## Product-Hodge input

The independently varying period domains supply the jointly Hodge-generic tuple with rank-two Néron–Severi groups, scalar transcendental endomorphisms and no pairwise transcendental Hodge isomorphisms. The chosen complex embedding is explicitly part of the data.

We verified the subdirect Lie-algebra argument in full. A proper subdirect semisimple Lie algebra would identify two \(\mathfrak{so}_{20}\) factors. In type \(D_{10}\), every diagram automorphism fixes the standard-vector highest weight. The representations would therefore have a nonzero intertwiner after scalar extension; the intertwiner equations are rational, so one exists over \(\mathbf Q\). Connectedness turns it into a Hodge isomorphism, contradicting the chosen tuple. Thus the Hodge group is the full product. The CM factor is independent because the derived group kills a torus and surjects onto the semisimple product.

For each nonempty transcendental support \(I\), the corresponding tensor representation with the CM elliptic \(H^1\) is rationally simple, after taking account of the two conjugate torus characters. The Néron–Severi factors and the three elliptic copies produce multiplicities. Every such constituent has level \(2|I|+1\ge3\). Hence the exact selected Künneth tensor has the asserted level-one part, uniformly for every parameter curve. This does not require the parameter curve to descend to \(\overline K\).

## Chern obstruction, source families and target witness

The three-section rank condition is nonempty: choose one linear form on each quartic whose multiplication does not kill its primitive \(\tau_\nu\), then use their product times the three curve coordinates. The generic section tuple satisfies this rank open and the independent geometric open simultaneously. The class and minors are defined algebraically over the countable coefficient field.

We checked the degree-\(r\) conormal exterior sequence, the rational Chern-character lift and the selected Künneth projection against the already audited C.3ae/C.3af arguments. Each factor's cohomological and differential degree is preserved, and the contraction acts only on the curve. The product-Hodge lemma reduces the relevant algebraic component to the Néron–Severi tensor, whose sole fully primitive line is killed by the rank-three obstruction. The source image is exactly \(\operatorname{pr}_{C,*}(\tau(b_0+ab_1))\); the \(ab_1\) term vanishes on the mixed component by the same missing-factor argument. Thus the image of every actual ordinary source-family difference is zero.

The target divisor construction uses legitimate line-bundle pullbacks even when the incidence projection is not flat. Its composite with \(\rho\) is \((-9)^s\) times the quotient map. Divisibility gives the integral cokernel surjection. The specified curve point with coordinate transcendental over \(\overline K\) has no nonzero multiple in \(\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)(\overline K)\); finite multiplication and the Abel closed immersion prove this. The target witness survives rationally.

## Exact primary source checks

The five K3/CM sources were independently read for C.3ag and are retained in that review: Brevik–Nollet, Huybrechts, Cattani–Deligne–Kaplan, Zarhin and Beauville, with the same exact locators and scope limitations.

For this audit we freshly opened the complete Milne *Reductive Groups*, version 2.00, 10 March 2018, and read 18.26–18.27 (pp. 91–92), 20.3–20.4 (pp. 102–103), 20.33 (p. 108) and 21.4 (p. 112). These are the precise root, highest-weight, integration and outer-automorphism inputs used above.

We also freshly opened Grothendieck's Bourbaki Exposé 221, the complete 29-page primary PDF, and read Theorems 3.1–3.2 (printed pp. 259–260), the projectivity argument (pp. 264–265), and the Hilbert specialization/universal-flat-family description (pp. 265–266). The separate 1962 erratum, printed p. 302, was opened and read. Its corrections do not remove or weaken the projective fixed-polynomial Hilbert scheme used here. The draft's field argument relies on these actual projective Hilbert schemes, not on an unsupported assertion about strict-local parameter spaces.

Let S=W×C be smooth of dimension3, M=O_W(1) external K_C, and a=c1(M).

## 1. Geometry: pass

Away from B, the kernel of O_U³→M_U is a rank2 bundle and H_U is its
P¹-bundle of lines. At b∈B the three ds_i form a basis of T*_bS after
trivializing M. At a point (x,b), the differential Σx_i ds_i is nonzero,
since x is a nonzero projective coordinate vector. Hence H is smooth
there as well. H_U is integral. Its complement P²×B has dimension2,
whereas H is a Cartier hypersurface of pure dimension4, so that complement
contains no component. Thus H is integral. The degree of B is M³=48.
The same equations show the strict-transform divisor and exceptional
zero section are transverse in the existing C.3ae construction.
The contraction, finite normalization, unique vertex, strict henselization,
and maximal-ideal pullback arguments are unchanged from that proof.

## 2. The integral CH1 decomposition needs no full Cayley trick

For every smooth parameter P, the complement of H_U×P in H×P has
codimension2. Localization therefore gives an isomorphism of CH¹ groups:
there are no codimension-one cycles supported in that complement.
The projective-bundle formula on H_U×P gives

    CH¹(H_U×P) = p* CH¹(U×P) ⊕ h p* CH⁰(U×P).

Removing B×P from S×P has codimension3, so localization likewise identifies
CH¹(U×P) with CH¹(S×P) and CH⁰(U×P) with CH⁰(S×P).
The displayed summands come from p* and h globally; consequently

    CH¹(H×P) = p* CH¹(S×P) ⊕ h p* CH⁰(S×P)

integrally. The argument is compatible with taking a parameter fibre.
This avoids any unverified application of a Cayley-trick decomposition in
higher codimensions. The exact localization and projective-bundle sources

finite-type schemes, within these sources' explicit scope.

In P²×S, the divisor class of H is h+a and h³=0. By pushing its
intersection with h^j through the ambient trivial P²-bundle, one obtains

    p_*1=0, p_*h=1, p_*h²=a, p_*h³=0.

There is no exceptional-fibre correction: these are identities computed
through the global Cartier embedding. For γ=γ0+hγ1 in CH¹(H×P),

## 6. Conditional Hodge representation argument and three-section rank

Assume the exact source input Hg(T_W)=SO(T_W), where T_W is the rational
transcendental K3 Hodge structure. Because H¹(C) is CM, the derived group
of Hg(T_W direct-sum H¹(C)) contains SO(T_W) acting trivially on H¹(C).
The standard SO representation is absolutely irreducible, so any rational
Hodge substructure of T_W tensor H¹(C) has the form T_W tensor U for a
rational subspace U of H¹(C). Stability under the Hodge circle makes U

zero. The algebraic component under consideration consequently lies in

requires no genericity condition chosen after P.

On a smooth quartic, the combined multiplication map
H¹(Ω¹_W)/C·H→H⁰(O_W(1))^* tensor H¹(Ω¹_W(1)) is injective: its dual is

generated in degree1. Hence for the nonzero primitive NS class τ there

condition is a different nonempty Zariski-open condition because M is
very ample. Their intersection is nonempty. The special triple proves
rank nonemptiness only and is not itself asserted to have a finite base
locus. This exact distinction is necessary.

# Independent full audit of C.3az

Reviewer: /root/real_weil, GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), ChatGPT Pro mode;
effort setting not exposed. Completed 2026-11-19T11:38:43.203963+00:00.
Reviewed entire agents/frobenius/C3_smooth_exceptional_top_draft.tex.
Outcome: PASS in exactly its stated algebraizable, characteristic-p,
single smooth exceptional Cartier divisor with ample conormal scope.
No mathematical correction is required. No computational program was
independently rerun as part of this review.

## Proof reconstruction

1. KST applies to the noetherian abstract blow-up square without any
resolution assumption. Both local K0 groups are Z, and quotient by
the graph of the structure sheaf leaves the claimed constant-pro
monomorphism. Its actual kernels are decreasing subgroups with
inclusion transitions, so pro-zero really implies a zero kernel at
one finite thickening. GH applies in every nonconnective degree;
finite affine Mayer-Vietoris descent globalizes the nilpotent
comparison after inverting p. No uniform exponent is needed.

2. The rational Chern-character argument has an appropriate finite
smooth model. Projectivity makes the image of the nonsmooth locus
closed; the selected closed fibre is regular, and over the perfect
coefficient field the finite-stage regularity/smoothness condition
spreads. Finite vector bundles, cycles and their relations descend.
Contravariant Chern character matches refined pullback without an
extra Todd factor. Injectivity of the full K0 map therefore gives
injectivity in each graded Chow degree. Actual curve families are
preserved by the refined Cartier pullback.

3. The surface W through the prescribed x,o is cut by sufficiently
positive relative sections. Serre vanishing lifts their restrictions
from E. Prescribed-point Bertini produces a smooth connected curve C;
the argument uses the geometric construction in Stacks45.8.3, not
its later prime-to-characteristic divisibility conclusion. Transverse
jets on E give a regular surface and regular sequence near C. Any
bad locus or extra component would have a nonempty proper closed
image in Spec R, hence meet the closed point, a contradiction.
The resulting W is integral because each component meets connected
C and distinct components of a regular scheme are disjoint.

4. At the nth Cartier thickening the ideal is exactly L_C^n.
On C times the entire proper parameter curve P, the obstruction is
H1(C,L_C^n) tensor H1(P,O_P). For the finitely many nonzero groups,
the pth tensor power kills the obstruction. All earlier restrictions
are raised simultaneously; a fixed finite exponent then suffices
for every later stage by Serre vanishing. This is a compatible
whole-family construction, not a pointwise lifting argument.

5. Cartier and base-adic ideals have cofinal powers. Projective GAGA
over Rhat algebraizes the whole family and its inverse; full
faithfulness verifies invertibility. Regular completion plus Popescu
allows descent of this actual line bundle to one smooth R-algebra.
The henselian lifting lemma supplies an R-point with the same residue

remaining degree. Injectivity, localization and self-intersection

ordinary quotient on Z, giving the ordinary quotient zero on X.

## Proof checks

1. **Smooth top weights.** For a smooth m-dimensional stratum over k=Fpbar, Levine's rational comparison identifies weight w of K_n with CH^w(-,n). The degree-n chain group vanishes if w>m+n. In weight m+n the chains are interior closed points of the n-cube over closed points of the stratum. Every such point is k-rational; proper pushforward from the point gives the asserted surjection from copies of CH^n(k,n). There are no chains in degree n-1, so this argument really applies to all cycles and then to their boundary quotient. Totaro's integral comparison identifies CH^n(k,n) with Milnor K_n(k). For n>0 its rationalization is zero because k* is torsion. The projective n=0 degree statement follows by a smooth projective curve through each pair of points and torsion of its finite-field-defined Jacobian points.

2. **Closed-union descent.** A union of SNC components has a reduced scheme-theoretic intersection in the decomposition used in the induction; the affine square is a Milnor square of surjective ring maps. Geisser--Hesselholt's Theorem C applies without a regularity assumption and in every integer degree. Thus the square of nonconnective K-theory spectra is cartesian after inverting p. TT open-cover descent globalizes the assertion.

3. **Adams operations: exact scope, with no regular-only shortcut.** Levine first describes Soule's sheaf operations for a regular scheme on p257. The next paragraph on p258 explicitly changes to Grayson's construction for an arbitrary scheme. It describes functoriality in the exact category of vector bundles, extension to any iterated homotopy fibre, agreement with the classical operations on K0, and delooping of the Adams operation. Apply this construction to the closed-union square itself; the connecting map is the homotopy-fibre boundary and therefore commutes with the same operation. There is no use of a support-to-subscheme devissage identification and hence no Thom/codimension weight shift. Lemma2.1 itself has regular-ambient/normal-crossing hypotheses. We do NOT apply that statement to the singular union. Instead we use the elementary Q[L]-module filtration argument proved at the beginning of its proof on p259: finite generalized-eigenspace decompositions are stable under the subquotients and extensions in the descent sequence. Induction from smooth strata supplies exactly the needed hypotheses. I requested that the owner make this source-scope distinction explicit; it is already the mathematical argument of the typed proof.

4. **SNC induction.** For C of dimension m-1, the predecessor K_(n+1)(C) in weight m+n is its top weight of a positive K-group and is zero. Above that weight it vanishes by the upper bound. At n=0 the end groups are K1(C) in weight m (top positive weight) and K0(C) in weight m (above dimension). Both vanish. This proves K0(E) in weight d is the direct sum of CH0 of the smooth components, hence Q^c. Empty/disconnected intersections do not affect the induction.

5. **Finite detection.** KST applies to the stated noetherian abstract blow-up square. The local K0 groups of R and its artinian quotients are Z. Quotienting their diagonal structure-sheaf graph leaves a constant pro-group K0(Z) mapping monomorphically to the thickening system. The kernels have inclusion transition maps, so pro-zero implies an actual finite-stage zero kernel. GH nilpotent invariance after inverting p then injects rational K0(Z) into K0(E). The finite smooth-model Chern-character comparison is the same previously checked input as C3az and is compatible with component restriction. Thus the component-degree map on CH^d(Z)_Q is injective. No identification of K with KH is used.

6. **Exceptional intersection matrix.** The matrix is symmetric because the same ample H restricts to both sides of each intersection. Off-diagonal entries are nonnegative. For the positive exceptional coefficient vector a, Ma has strictly negative coordinates because -D is ample on each component. The displayed weighted energy identity proves negative definiteness without requiring a connected dual complex. The exceptional complete-intersection curves therefore span all component degree vectors. Combined with injectivity this gives the exact claimed isomorphism and Chow localization kills the entire top Chow group of the puncture.

## 1. Exact scope checked

Let (R,m,k) be an excellent henselian local domain, k isomorphic to Fpbar, and dim R=N>=2. There is no normality, finite-type-model, equal-characteristic, or regular-puncture assumption on R. The proved groups are

    CH_1(Spec R)_Q = 0,
    CH^{N-1}(Spec R minus {m})_Q = 0.

The dimension function is delta(p)=dim(R/p) and is restricted unchanged to the puncture. Since a catenary local domain has ht(p)+dim(R/p)=N, the displayed codimension index is correct; deleting the closed point is not a reason to replace N by the puncture's smaller Krull dimension. The ordinary quotient is asserted only where its equivalence convention is defined. In particular the text does not impose coefficient-field product families on a mixed-characteristic ring.

The result does not assert integral vanishing or a uniform annihilating integer. It does not extend the residue field to an arbitrary transcendental algebraically closed field. Those distinctions are explicit and necessary.

## 2. Surface geometry checked

For a normal excellent local surface B, normality supplies a regular puncture, and excellence gives normal completion. Stacks54.14.5 applies with its exact condition (4), and its proof together with54.6.5 supplies normalized closed-point blowups over the singular closed point. Finite normalization is ensured by excellence. These modifications are projective and preserve the puncture simultaneously. In the regular case, the first modification is the blowup of the closed point.

Embedded resolution of the entire closed fibre uses Stacks54.15.6 on a regular surface; finite normalization of its curve components follows from excellence. Its proof uses closed-point blowups supported on that fibre. The final reduced fibre E is a projective strict normal-crossings curve; each component is smooth over the perfect residue field k. This reasoning does not import the threefold resolution theorem or its affine-cover projectivity issue.

The effective exceptional divisor with ample negative is also constructed, not presumed. For an ordinary blowup the exceptional F is effective Cartier and O(-F)=O(1). Pullback to a finite normalization remains Cartier because the normalization is dominant between integral schemes; finite pullback preserves relative ampleness, checked locally over an affine open of the preceding stage. For a subsequent step h, the divisor F_h+a h*D_0 is effective and its negative is ample for the composite once a is sufficiently large. This is exactly the sign in Stacks29.38.8. The first exceptional divisor has the entire first closed fibre as support, so its total transform ensures every final exceptional component occurs with a positive coefficient. No unproved conjunction of projectivity and regular-open preservation remains.

## 3. Finite K0 detection and determinant checked

KST TheoremA/(1.6) applies to the noetherian abstract blowup square with centre the closed point. K0(B) and K0(B/n^b) are Z. Quotienting the diagonal graph of the structure-sheaf class leaves the constant pro-group K0(Z), which maps monomorphically to the system K0(E_b). The levelwise kernel groups are decreasing subgroups of that fixed group, with inclusion transition maps. A pro-zero system of inclusions has an actually zero term. Thus some finite thickening detects K0(Z); no inference from vanishing of an inverse limit alone is used.

The mixed-characteristic extension is justified exactly: p lies in n, hence p^b=0 on E_b. Geisser--Hesselholt TheoremA printedp29 assumes p is nilpotent in the ring, not that the ring is an Fp-algebra. On each affine of the finite detecting thickening, the nilpotent reduction to E is therefore a K-equivalence after inverting p. A finite affine cover and Thomason--Trobaugh Zariski descent give the rational K0 comparison globally. No p-nilpotence on B or Z is asserted.

For a line bundle L of multidegree zero on E, the normalization/gluing argument is valid. Each component restriction is a point of a Jacobian over Fpbar and is torsion; after a common power trivializes these restrictions, only finitely many node-gluing scalars remain. They lie in k* and are torsion. A further power makes the restriction actually trivial on E, even if the dual graph has several connected components.

Consequently [L^M]-[O_Z] is zero in K0(E), hence zero rationally in K0(Z). Some integer multiple is zero integrally in K0(Z). The determinant homomorphism then gives L^{Mn}=O_Z. The proof correctly takes an actual tensor power before applying K0; it does not confuse the additive class [L]-1 with the assertion that L has finite tensor order. Z is projective over affine and has the resolution property; Stacks36.38.5 identifies perfect-complex and vector-bundle K0, and Stacks17.26/17.26.1 gives the required determinant map. M_ij=deg(O_Z(E_j)|E_i) is symmetric, with nonnegative off-diagonal intersection lengths. The effective divisor D=Σa_iE_i with -D ample gives Ma<0. With Q=diag(a)Mdiag(a), the identity

is exact. It proves negative definiteness and invertibility. The exceptional line bundles consequently span all rational multidegrees and, by injectivity, all Pic(Z)_Q. Taking the Weil-divisor closure of a Cartier divisor on the regular puncture supplies Pic(Z)→Pic(U) surjectivity; Z is regular and locally factorial. Exceptional bundles restrict trivially. Hence Pic(U)_Q=0.

For the normal local surface, CH_1(Spec B)→CH_1(U)=Pic(U) is an isomorphism by localization: the closed point has delta-dimension zero, so carries no one-cycles. This surface conclusion has exactly the arbitrary-excellent henselian and mixed-characteristic scope needed later.

For each curve prime p of the possibly nonnormal domain R, a saturated chain from0 to m through p has a preceding prime q with dim(R/q)=2. Catenarity supplies the exact lengths; N=2 is handled by q=0. The quotient R/q is an excellent henselian local domain. Its normalization T is finite by excellence and remains a domain. Integral extension preserves dimension, so T is a normal local surface to which the preceding argument applies. No algebraization or simultaneous descent of q and its normalization is necessary.

A prime P above p/q is neither zero nor maximal: its contraction is nonzero and nonmaximal. In dimension2 it is therefore height1. The composite Spec T→Spec(R/q)→Spec R is finite. Rational equivalences are preserved, so the surface vanishing kills each ambient curve generator rationally. Localization removes the closed point without changing CH_1. This proves the all-N claim without a resolution theorem in dimension>N=2.
